chapters.title: Chapter 101 -100-Intermediate Divinity Fragment, Immortal Singularity
paragraphs: Boom—!
With the final point of Immortal Singularity exhausted, Harland’s body finally exploded amid the endless thunderstorm, bursting into fragments that filled the sky.
Those fragments burned in the lightning, broke apart, and turned to ashes, leaving not even the slightest trace behind.
[Ding! You have slain the Legendary-Grade powerhouse "Fallen Mage Harland" and gained +50 billion EXP!]
[Prompt: Your current EXP pool is full. Overflow EXP has been automatically stored.]
[Ding! "Plunderer" effect triggered! The enemy’s dropped items have been automatically transferred to your inventory!]
[Prompt: You have completed the quest "Plaguefall" (Epic-Grade)! Quest Rating: Perfect!]
[Ding! Obtained "Purification Elixir" (Epic-Grade) ×1!]
[Ding! Obtained "Judgment Elixir" (Epic-Grade) ×1!]
[Ding! Obtained "Intermediate Divinity Fragment" (Legendary-Grade · Special Item, Unsellable) ×1!]
A slight flicker passed through Daniel’s eyes as he listened to the system notifications.
Of the three dropped items, two were actually potions. That was rather unexpected.
Still, potions could trigger the bonus effect of the Eternal Ring and become permanent effects, so it counted as a pleasant surprise.
As for that Divinity Fragment, that was the real prize.
A powerhouse who had only just stepped into the threshold of Legendary-Grade had actually dropped an Intermediate Divinity Fragment?!
By any standard, this was an enormous profit.
Divinity Fragments were the core material used to synthesize a complete Divinity. It took one hundred fragments to form a single complete Divinity.
And a complete Divinity was precisely the key item needed for a player’s class advancement quest after reaching Level 200.
The more Divinity consumed during class advancement, and the higher its rank, the more terrifying the strength gained after advancement would be.
He put the fragment into his inventory, then took out the two potions and sold them to the guild.
[Ding! You have successfully sold "Judgment Elixir" and "Purification Elixir" to the Doom Guild, receiving 2 copper coins!]
[Ding! Millionfold Boost triggered. Please choose: Quantity Boost / Quality Boost!]
"Quality Boost!"
[Ding! Congratulations! You have received 2 gold coins! Congratulations! You have obtained Sacred Judgment Elixir (Supreme-Grade) and Holy Light Purification Elixir (Supreme-Grade)!]
Delight stirred in Daniel’s heart as he opened the potion panel to inspect them.
[Sacred Judgment Elixir (Legendary-Grade)]
Effect: After consumption, damage dealt to dark-aligned creatures is increased tenfold.
Duration: 12 hours
Description: When darkness shrouds the world, you shall be the light that tears it apart and passes judgment upon evil.
Daniel’s breathing paused for the briefest moment.
Ten times damage!
After drinking this potion, his damage output against dark-aligned creatures would soar to over fifty million.
Those dark calamities destined to descend in the future...
Those shadow creatures that would blanket the skies...
Those fiends that would devour the light...
With a tenfold damage bonus, they would no longer be invincible nightmares!
He tipped his head back and drank the potion in one gulp.
The golden liquid slid down his throat, like molten sunlight flowing through his veins.
[Prompt: You have consumed "Sacred Judgment Elixir" (Supreme-Grade)!]
[Ding! Talent "Eternal Ring" triggered! The potion’s effect has been converted into a permanent effect!]
He then looked at the other potion in his hand.
[Holy Light Purification Elixir (Supreme-Grade)]
Effect: After consumption, grants the continuous ability to remove all negative statuses and toxins.
Duration: 12 hours
Description: Dispel all evil, cleanse away every burden; remain pure and clear in body, forever free of curses.
The corner of Daniel’s lips lifted slightly.
Although he already had plenty of purification methods on him and could long since ignore debuffs altogether, an extra safeguard was always welcome.
From this moment onward, no curse, toxin, or negative status would be able to remain on him for more than an instant.
He drank the potion down in a single swallow.
[Prompt: You have consumed "Holy Light Purification Elixir" (Supreme-Grade)!]
[Ding! Talent "Eternal Ring" triggered! The potion’s effect has been converted into a permanent effect!]
Daniel put away the potions and turned his gaze toward the place where Harland had fallen.
A few scorched scraps of cloth lay scattered across the blackened ground, with thin wisps of smoke curling upward into the night wind.
Though this fallen mage had only been at the very bottom among Legendary-Grade existences, he had still been a true Legendary-Grade powerhouse.
Daniel had no intention of reviving him, but keeping the corpse might prove useful for something else.
He spread the Eternal Black King and descended to the place where Harland had fallen.
But the instant he landed, a cold and sinister aura rose from the ruins.
The remaining fragments of Harland’s corpse trembled slightly, and an aged voice emerged from within them, like a murmur drifting up from an unimaginably distant abyss.
"Was it you who killed Harland?"
The voice was hoarse and low, carrying an unsettling pressure.
"You have chosen to become an enemy of the Shadow Council... have you considered the consequences?"
Daniel frowned faintly and said coldly,
"If I’m not mistaken, you’re Harland’s mentor, aren’t you?"
"A peak Legendary-Grade powerhouse of the dark magic lineage—the one with the highest bounty on the Empire’s wanted list."
The voice in the ruins fell silent for a moment, then turned into a cold laugh.
"So what?"
"Nothing much."
Daniel spoke calmly, in a tone as though he were merely stating a fact long since set in stone.
"I just wanted to tell you that you’re going to die too. And when you do, it’ll be ugly."
He was telling the truth.
This peak powerhouse of the Shadow Council before him would, in the end, still be suppressed by humanity’s strongest.
Viewed from a higher plane, his death was only a matter of time.
The voice fell silent for a long while.
Then a burst of deranged laughter exploded from the ruins, shaking even the scattered stones.
"Ha ha ha... sooner or later, you will understand that everything you are doing for the Empire now is utterly futile."
"The cycle of rebirth never ends—why should death be feared? When I die, it will be the day I enter the divine kingdom!"
The moment the words fell—
Boom!
Harland’s remains exploded into utter ruin in an instant, leaving behind not even a single grain of dust.
Daniel gazed at that barren patch of scorched earth, his eyes cold as frost.
He paid no heed to the wild ravings of that Shadow Council mentor.
He only knew one thing: he had to make haste in laying the groundwork for mankind’s future.
No matter what kind of disasters awaited ahead, he would fear none of them!
"Time to go back and turn in the quest."
He murmured softly, then spread his wings and shot into the sky.
Luminara, Ministry of War.
A black shadow dived down from the clouds and landed steadily in the square before the Ministry of War.
When the surrounding soldiers saw who it was, they immediately straightened their backs, placed their right fists against their chests, and looked at him with eyes full of reverence.
"Your Grace!"
Daniel nodded and strode into the great hall of the Ministry.

Kasel had already noticed his arrival. He looked Daniel up and down several times, and only after confirming that there was not even a single wound on him did he finally let out a long breath of relief.
Daniel smiled faintly and briefly recounted what had happened with Harland and Harland’s mentor.
After hearing it all, Kasel’s eyes filled with astonishment.
"To think that Your Grace was able to slay a Legendary-Grade powerhouse alone—truly extraordinary!"
He paused, his expression growing grave once more.
"As for the one behind the scenes... Your Grace need not worry too much. The Empire has its own ways of dealing with him."
He waved a hand broadly.
[Ding! You have submitted the quest "Plaguefall" (Epic-Grade)! Quest Rating: Perfect!]
[Obtained rewards: Immortal Singularity Fragment (Legendary-Grade) ×1, +1 billion gold coins, +1 billion merit points, +50,000 Human Merit, +100,000 Imperial Morale!]
Daniel was briefly stunned.
These rewards could only be described as top-tier.
[Immortal Singularity Fragment] was the core material used to synthesize Immortal Singularity.
Gather one hundred of them, and they could be condensed into one point of Immortal Singularity.
And one point of Immortal Singularity meant one chance to negate death.
Moreover, Immortal Singularity could also be channeled into offensive skills, greatly increasing their power.
If he had possessed Immortal Singularity during that battle, an opponent on Harland’s level would never have lasted more than a few exchanges.

chapters.title: Chapter 102 -102-Polaris Sets Its Sights on Everfrost
paragraphs: Polaris City.
No sooner had Daniel settled into the Lord’s Manor than a blood-red world announcement resounded across the entire world of Stellar.
[Server-Wide Announcement!!!]
[The six races—beastfolk, dwarves, elves, goblins, Bimon, and mammoths—have declared the formation of the "Sixfold Alliance" and officially declared war on the Human Empire!]
[Declaration of the Six Races]
"The humans know no justice. They crossed our borders, burned our city-states, slaughtered our people, and seized our lands. Their hands are drenched in blood!"
"Today, our six races stand shoulder to shoulder. We seek not conquest, but only the return of all that was taken from its rightful owners!"
"The tyranny of humankind shall fall. Their walls shall crumble. Their rule shall come to an end. By blood and blade, we swear to fight until the final shadow has faded."
[Server-Wide Announcement: A major version event has now begun! Players who participate in this event may earn massive rewards! All players, prepare yourselves!]
The announcement rang out three times in succession. Crimson text flashed before every player’s eyes, like a declaration of war written in blood.
The World Channel instantly exploded.
"Another version storyline? Why is it advancing so fast?!"
"By the gods, I’m only level twenty and I already have to take part in a major version event?"
"I don’t think this has anything to do with our levels. It’s because someone has already reached that stage! Faustus is just completely insane!"
"This feels a little rough. One against six? That’s a headache."

"What’s there to be afraid of? During the Battle of Desperation, Faustus slaughtered hundreds of millions of players and tens of billions of monsters all by himself! How could these non-human races be any stronger?"
"You’re underestimating them. All six major races have huge numbers of legendary-grade powerhouses! Did that secret realm even have legendary-grade enemies?"
"Hiss... if that’s true, then this really is huge."
"It’s definitely a serious challenge, but still! There’s no way players are going to be the main force in a war on this scale... unless you’re Faustus."
"Uh... fair point!"
Standing atop the high platform of the Lord’s Manor, Daniel gazed toward the roiling storm clouds gathering in the northern sky.
A faint smile curved at his lips.
With the main armies of the non-human races concentrated in the north, this was actually good news for him.
That vast stretch of the Ironhammer Plains would become his hunting ground.
Daniel was not at all surprised by the Sixfold Alliance’s declaration of war.
Scouts from the non-human races had already been making restless moves along the border. Now that their army stood beneath Everwinter City, all they had done was tear away the final veil.
War had only ever been a matter of time.
He took his seat at the head of the hall, pondered for a moment, then opened the mission editor.
His fingers traced one command after another through the air, every parameter weighed and reconsidered again and again.
A moment later, he confirmed the release.
A golden announcement burst before the eyes of every player in World Zone 616.
[World Zone 616 Announcement: Player "Faustus" has issued the world quest "War Edict"! Pay 100 copper coins to qualify for the quest!]
The announcement sounded three times in a row.
The World Channel erupted once more.
"By the gods! Faustus is making his move!"
"Take it! Take it! Take it! If Faustus is involved, you can accept it with your eyes closed!"
"Exactly! The big guy gets the meat, and if we’re lucky, we can at least drink some soup!"
Countless players rushed to pay the copper coins and sign up, not even bothering to read the quest details first.
Only after a line of golden text appeared in their quest logs did they finally see the full contents of the War Edict.
[War Edict] (Issued by Faustus)
Quest Difficulty: SSS-Rank
Quest Objective: Exterminate all non-human races on sight
Quest Description: The non-human races have invaded. Let all humanity strike back together. Any player in World Zone 616 may kill any non-human race or non-human player on sight.
Quest Duration: Long-term
Quest Rewards: For every non-human race or non-human player killed, receive 20 silver coins / 2 merit points / 200 quest EXP
At the same time, the system notifications at Daniel’s ear poured down like a torrential storm.
[Ding! Millionfold Boost triggered! Gold coins +100!]
[Ding! Millionfold Boost triggered! Gold coins +100!]
[Ding! Millionfold Boost triggered! Gold coins +100!]
The players’ enthusiasm for purchasing quest qualification was unbelievably high.
Daniel glanced at his wealth value. In just a few moments, it had already broken through the ten-billion mark.
And the number was still climbing at a speed visible to the naked eye.
Daniel muted the notifications and summoned all the high-ranking commanders of his legions.
Inside the council hall, candlelight stretched every shadow long across the floor.
Hudson, Victor, Alan, Aliris... every face was solemn and resolute.
Daniel briefly informed them of the Sixfold Alliance’s declaration of war.
The hall fell silent for a moment, then was quickly engulfed by a heavy, suppressed fighting spirit.
Hudson was the first to rise, his voice steady as iron.

"My lord duke, the Polaris Legion currently numbers eleven million soldiers, while the Doom Legion has fifty-five million. We possess one epic-grade legion, one legendary-grade legion, and countless elite forces. That strength is enough to deal with any non-human race."
Daniel nodded, his gaze sweeping across every person present.
"The main forces of the non-human races are currently tied down at the northern fortress, locked in confrontation with the imperial army."
His voice was not loud, yet every word carried clearly to everyone in the chamber.
"Our target... is the beastfolk main city—Everfrost!"
Victor’s eyes lit up.
"The beastfolk have transferred all of their elite forces to the northern front. Everfrost must be badly undermanned right now."
"If we can take it in one stroke, not only will we relieve the Empire’s pressure, we’ll also drive a nail into this plain."
"Exactly."
Daniel rose to his feet and walked to the enormous map hanging on the wall, then pressed a finger against the location marked Everfrost.
"You are to draft a detailed battle plan centered around this main city. Within one day, I want to see a complete proposal."
"Yes, sir!"
Everyone answered in unison.
Daniel turned back, his gaze sweeping over every face once more.
Candlelight danced in his eyes, as though some ancient flame were burning there.
"The non-human races have never abandoned their desire to destroy our human kind!"
His voice was low, but full of force.
"It is our duty to fight for the protection of our people."
At once, every commander in the hall rose to their feet and placed a clenched fist over the chest.
"For humanity!"
One day later.
Outside Polaris City, a dark mass of troops stretched to the horizon.
Sixty-five million NPC warriors stood in formation, their armor gleaming with a cold metallic sheen beneath the morning light.
Behind them stood millions of ordinary players. Some rode warhorses, some led hunting hounds, some carried giant bows nearly as tall as they were, and some leaned on rune-inlaid staves.
The same battle intent burned in every pair of eyes.
Standing atop the city wall, Daniel looked down upon this iron tide that he had built with his own hands.
"Move out."
The grand army began its march.
The road from Polaris City to Everfrost turned out to be unexpectedly smooth.
The beastfolk had clearly adopted a scorched-earth and defensive consolidation strategy, pulling all scattered populations and military forces back into their main city.
Along the way, apart from scattered wild beasts and routed scouts, they encountered no resistance of any meaningful scale.
Only after half a day’s march did the outline of Everfrost appear on the horizon.

"If we can take it in one stroke, not only will we relieve the Empire’s pressure, we’ll also drive a nail into this plain."
"Exactly."
Daniel rose to his feet and walked to the enormous map hanging on the wall, then pressed a finger against the location marked Everfrost.
"You are to draft a detailed battle plan centered around this main city.
Within one day, I want to see a complete proposal."
"Yes, sir!"
Everyone answered in unison.
Daniel turned back, his gaze sweeping over every face once more.
Candlelight danced in his eyes, as though some ancient flame were burning there.
"The non-human races have never abandoned their desire to destroy our human kind!"
His voice was low, but full of force.
"It is our duty to fight for the protection of our people."
At once, every commander in the hall rose to their feet and placed a clenched fist over the chest.
"For humanity!"
One day later.
Outside Polaris City, a dark mass of troops stretched to the horizon.
Sixty-five million NPC warriors stood in formation, their armor gleaming with a cold metallic sheen beneath the morning light.
Behind them stood millions of ordinary players.
Some rode warhorses, some led hunting hounds, some carried giant bows nearly as tall as they were, and some leaned on rune-inlaid staves.
The same battle intent burned in every pair of eyes.
Standing atop the city wall, Daniel looked down upon this iron tide that he had built with his own hands.
"Move out."
The grand army began its march.
The road from Polaris City to Everfrost turned out to be unexpectedly smooth.
The beastfolk had clearly adopted a scorched-earth and defensive consolidation strategy, pulling all scattered populations and military forces back into their main city.
Along the way, apart from scattered wild beasts and routed scouts, they encountered no resistance of any meaningful scale.
Only after half a day’s march did the outline of Everfrost appear on the horizon.

chapters.title: Chapter 103 -103-Finishing Blow — Slaying a Legendary-Grade Powerhouse
paragraphs: Everfrost!
It was a colossal city built against the mountains. Its gray stone walls rose more than thirty meters high, their surfaces carved all over with ancient beastfolk war totems.
The top of the walls was packed shoulder to shoulder with beastfolk warriors—wolfkin, bearfolk, minotaurs...
They gripped battle axes and giant hammers, low growls rumbling from their throats.
The entire city had gathered tens of millions of beastfolk within it.
And deep in the heart of the city, an aura that sent chills down the spine lay hidden like a dormant volcano, restrained but ready to erupt.
That was the aura of a legendary-grade powerhouse!
Outside the city, Daniel’s army had formed up in battle lines. War drums rose and fell without pause, and banners snapped violently in the wind.
Everyone was waiting for that signal to charge.
Inside the command tent.
Daniel stood before the sand table, with Carodion and Aliris at his side.
He was silent for a moment, then turned his gaze toward Carodion.
The revived peak legendary-grade warrior stood quietly to one side, like a sheathed blade—silent, yet razor-sharp.
"Carodion,"
Daniel finally said, "once the battle begins, your task is to heavily wound the beastfolk legendary-grade expert. Weaken him to the limit, then leave the killing blow to me."
Carodion gave a slight nod, his voice as calm as still water.
"As you command, my lord."
Daniel nodded.

The last time he had faced Harland, he had not possessed the strength to instantly kill a legendary-grade powerhouse. He had only been able to grind him down to death through an endless barrage of skills.
But on a battlefield, he would not have that kind of time or space.
Let Carodion strike first and reduce the enemy to critical condition, then step in and finish him off himself—this was the safest plan.
Daniel drew a deep breath and stepped out of the command tent.
Sixty-five million soldiers had already completed their formation.
The clash of sword and shield, the tapping of staves against the earth, the snorting and pawing of warhorses—all of it wove together into a low, solemn prelude to war.
Under the watch of all, Daniel raised a hand.
"Full army, attack."
Beneath Everfrost.
The human army, numbering in the tens of millions, surged forward like a rising tide.
Orders rolled from the rear to the front in wave after wave, like surf crashing against rock.
"Archer regiments—prepare volley fire!"
"Mage regiments—begin chanting!"
The sound of bowstrings being drawn filled the battlefield, like ten thousand great birds beating their wings at once.
The mages raised their staffs high. Elemental power gathered at the tips, warping the air itself from the heat.
"Siege corps—fire!"
Whoosh! Whoosh! Whoosh!
Countless advanced trebuchets launched in unison, hurling burning projectiles and massive ballista bolts toward Everfrost like a torrential storm.
The walls, painstakingly built by beastfolk craftsmen, shook violently under the bombardment of steel and flame, smoke and dust billowing everywhere.
Screams rang out from atop the walls. Some beastfolk were sent tumbling down from the battlements, some were pinned through by giant bolts, while others were swallowed by fire.
After just three volleys, that once unshakable beastfolk stronghold was already on the verge of collapse!
The beastfolk had long since transferred most of their war machines to the northern front, leaving the city with almost no meaningful means of retaliation.
All they could do was stand atop the walls and use their flesh and blood to endure the baptism of steel and fire.
"Humans—you truly are insatiably greedy!"
A furious roar erupted from the depths of the city.
A gigantic figure shot into the sky, carrying a pressure great enough to ruin heaven and earth as it plunged toward the human battle lines.
A legendary-grade powerhouse!
Yet the formation of the human legions did not shift in the slightest.
The archers continued firing. The mages continued chanting.
It was as if that approaching shadow of death did not exist at all.
Because they knew someone would stop him.
Daniel unfurled the Eternal Black King and shot into the sky.
At the same moment, Carodion turned into a streak of golden light and slammed head-on into the beastfolk figure.
Boom—!
The power of two legendary-grade experts exploded across the heavens, the shockwave shredding the clouds for miles around.
Carodion’s longsword and the beastfolk powerhouse’s battle axe clashed again and again, each collision bursting with dazzling sparks.
In theory, human warriors were usually weaker than beastfolk when fighting opponents of the same tier.
After all, beastfolk were born for battle.
But Carodion was at the peak of legendary-grade, while the golden-furred beastfolk opponent before him was only mid-tier.
That gulf in strength was enough to crush any racial advantage.
After only a few exchanges, the beastfolk expert was sent flying by Carodion’s sword, blood scattering across the sky.
Daniel did not spare a glance for that legendary-grade duel.

His eyes were fixed on Everfrost. Large numbers of beastfolk elites were pouring out from the city, trying to bypass the terrifying clash of those two legendary-grade powers and destroy his side’s war machines.
Daniel let out a cold laugh.
God Speed!
His figure flickered across the battlefield again and again, and every appearance was accompanied by fifty golden arrows of light.
Those arrows swept through the ranks of beastfolk elites like the scythes of death, carving bloody paths straight through them.
Epic-grade beastfolk warriors were like paper dolls before him. One arrow pierced through them, and their corpses dropped from the sky.
Even the beastfolk commanders at the legendary-grade level did not have time to see where the arrows had come from before they were torn apart by golden light.
In just a few short minutes, dozens of beastfolk powerhouses had all fallen!
On the battlefield, the players stared at the scene with mouths wide enough to fit a fist.
"By the gods... this is Faustus’s strength?"
"This is outrageous! Those epic-grade experts look like they’re made of paper!"
"Six or seven million damage! Who the hell can tank that? Drop that into our camp and whole groups would die instantly!"
"Why do I feel like... Faustus and I aren’t even playing the same game?"
"Why do you think there’s only one player called a god?"
After slaughtering all the beastfolk elites, Daniel turned midair and flew toward the region where Carodion and the beastfolk legendary-grade expert were battling.
The aftershocks from the clash of two legendary-grade powers were enough to tear any epic-grade powerhouse to pieces.
Yet Daniel passed through that zone of death without changing expression.
By now, his HP, defense, and regeneration had long surpassed the boundaries of normal understanding.
Not to mention, he still had methods of nullifying fatal damage.
The moment he drew near the beastfolk expert, Daniel raised Stellar Wrath.
[Wind’s Embrace]!
An invisible force of wind surged in from all directions, binding the blood-soaked beastfolk legendary-grade expert in place.
His body froze in midair, like an insect trapped in amber.
The beastfolk expert was both shocked and enraged!
He was already struggling to hold out against Carodion. Now that he had been bound by a human spell, was he not nothing more than meat on the chopping block?
A sharp gleam flashed through Carodion’s eyes.
He raised the longsword in his hand high overhead. A hundred-meter-long golden blade aura condensed along the edge, like divine punishment falling from the heavens.
The sword fell!
The beastfolk expert’s body was cleaved into two halves by a single strike.
But under the protection of Immortal Singularity, the severed flesh and blood rapidly fused back together.
Though he barely preserved his life, only a sliver of health remained.
Daniel lifted a hand.
[Serpent’s Thundercell]!
Boom—!

Dark clouds gathered in an instant. Purple lightning poured down like a storm, transforming into tens of thousands of thunder-serpents that tore madly into the nearly dead beastfolk legendary-grade powerhouse.
The last remnant of Immortal Singularity inside the beastfolk expert had already been completely exhausted by Carodion’s sword strike.
Against such horrifying damage, he did not last even a second before turning to ashes within the lightning.
[Ding! You have killed the beastfolk legendary-grade powerhouse "Bloodaxe Gonon"! EXP +100 billion! Gold coins +1.8 billion!]
[Obtained "Intermediate Divinity Fragment (Legendary-Grade)" ×1!]
[Obtained "Raging Iron Armor (Legendary-Grade)" ×1!]

chapters.title: Chapter 104 -104-The Human Powerhouses Being Toyed With
paragraphs: A faint smile touched Daniel’s lips.
Another Intermediate Divinity Fragment!
With the one that had dropped from Harland before, he was now one step closer to forging a complete Divinity.
And then there was that legendary-grade armor, along with all the equipment that had dropped earlier from the beastfolk epic-grade and legendary-grade elites.
From this single battle alone, he had gained at least fifty pieces of gear above the epic-grade level, including more than ten legendary-grade items!
He opened the equipment interface and selected weapon enhancement.
[Prompt: Consume ten legendary-grade items to upgrade "Stellar Wrath"? This action is irreversible!]
"Confirm."
[Ding! "Stellar Wrath" has successfully devoured ten legendary-grade items! Current Level: Lv.10!]
Daniel opened the weapon panel.
[Stellar Wrath (Supreme-Grade)]
Level: 10
Trait: Growth-Type
Equipment Effects:
Agility +1000 (previously +500) Grants skill [Starveil]: Summons a starlight shield that absorbs 1,000,000 damage. While the shield exists, the user is immune to all control effects.
III. Whenever a forbidden-grade skill is cast, its effect is doubled.
All archer-class skill effects +200% (previously +100%)
Durability: Infinite
Description:

A supreme-grade masterpiece forged in the final years of the legendary Arrow God Aranas. It contains the boundless source power of the stars themselves. Every pattern etched into the bow records a lost spell, and every arrow it fires can call down heavenly punishment and tear apart the firmament.
Daniel closed the panel and opened his status window.
With the stacking of hundreds of buffs, equipment bonuses, and Skill Replication, his base damage output had already broken past the seven-million mark!
The effect of the [Fate Stone] made every single one of his attacks equivalent to the damage of his strongest skill.
That meant that even an ordinary basic shot could deal over seventy million damage!
This level of damage output was simply monstrous.
Daniel and Carodion hovered high in the air, looking down upon Everfrost below them.
The beastfolk warriors in the city were still putting up a desperate resistance, but the fall of their legendary-grade powerhouse had already determined the outcome of the battle.
The morale of the beastfolk had completely collapsed. Some dropped to their knees and surrendered. Some tried to break out. Some charged madly toward the human battle lines.
"May the Beast God protect us! Brothers, charge!"
"The Beast God is with us—crush these invaders!"
"The beastfolk will never be slaves!!"
Daniel watched it all with an indifferent expression.
If not for the fact that these beastfolk made excellent laborers, he might truly have ordered a massacre.
"Hudson."
His voice was calm as still water.
"Spare those who surrender. Kill all who resist."
"Send every beastfolk willing to surrender to the mines."
Hudson bowed.
"As you command, my lord duke."
"And one more thing," Daniel added. "Have the priest corps on standby at all times, ready to resurrect any fallen warriors."
The battle for Everfrost came to an end at dusk.
In this war, the human army’s casualties were negligible.
Under overwhelming superiority of force and a complete resurrection system, death was nothing more than a brief pause.
The gains, on the other hand, were astonishing.
Daniel opened the post-battle report, his eyes quickly sweeping across the numbers.
1.3 million beastfolk prisoners, most of them wounded.
Supplies, ore, and equipment of every kind were piled up like mountains. Gold coins alone were worth hundreds of billions.
[Ding! Obtained "Gold Mine (Legendary-Grade)" ×1!]
[Ding! Obtained "Silver Mine (Epic-Grade)" ×1!]
The corners of Daniel’s mouth lifted slightly.
War profiteering really was the fastest road to riches.
Daniel closed the interface and lifted his gaze toward the distant horizon.
Ironforge had been the first main city he conquered. Everfrost was the second.
One in the south, one in the north—like two wedges hammered deep into the heartland of the non-human races!
Next, his target would be the elves!
Northern Great Wall, Winterhold.
While Daniel was laying siege to cities in the south, the war in the north had already entered its most brutal phase.
A city wall that stretched for tens of thousands of miles and rose a hundred meters high cut across the mountain range like a scar that split the world in two.
Winterhold sat at the most critical pass, wrapped in layer upon layer of magical barriers like a giant beast curled inside its shell.
Nearly a trillion soldiers of the Sixfold Host were arrayed beneath the walls, their countless banners blotting out the sky and the sun.
Hundreds of thousands of siege weapons fired at once, flaming shells and massive bolts pouring toward the fortress like a storm.
Yet when assaults powerful enough to erase ordinary cities struck the magical barriers, they produced only ripples of light before vanishing into nothing.
Boom—!
At last, one layer of the barrier shattered under the unending bombardment.
The Sixfold Host erupted in thunderous cheers.
"Excellent! The humans are finally running short on resources!"
"Roar, roar, roar—crush those insects up there!"
"May the Elven God bless us!"
"Victory is ours!"
That shattered barrier was quickly filled in by a fresh new layer of light rising from behind it.
But the blood-maddened warriors of the Sixfold Host only grew more excited.
A thousand miles beyond Winterhold.
Another war was unfolding in a land shrouded by a bizarre and terrifying force.
Across a thousand-mile radius, space itself twisted and warped. Mist swirled everywhere, as though someone had torn open a crack to another world upon this land.
Dozens of figures were crossing and clashing within this Godscar, every collision unleashing enough force to destroy a city.
The human side had only a little over ten legendary-grade powerhouses.
Opposing them, the Sixfold Host had more than twenty.
The numerical gap was only barely offset by the humans’ perfect coordination and tacit teamwork.
Barely.
Boom—!
A violent blast of power forced an old man on the human side back several steps.
Montague, the peak legendary-grade beastfolk expert, withdrew his fist, swept his gaze across the field, and suddenly shouted:
"Stop!"
At his command, the legendary-grade experts of the six races immediately disengaged from battle and gathered around him with practiced precision.
Montague cast a cold glance at the human powerhouses opposite him, the corner of his mouth curling into a disdainful sneer.
"We’ll spare your miserable lives for today. Retreat!"
Before the echo of his voice had even faded, more than twenty figures withdrew like a receding tide, vanishing over the horizon in the blink of an eye.
The human powerhouses stared in the direction they had gone, their expressions grave.
"This isn’t normal."
A weak voice came from the crowd.
The priest Tiana leaned against a broken stone pillar, her face pale as paper, but a sharp light still burned in her eyes.
"Haven’t any of you noticed?"
Though her voice was weak, each word came through with complete clarity.
"Every time the balance of the situation starts to tip like this, they withdraw on their own."
"Fuck—these damned non-human races. Do they really think our human race is easy prey?"
One of the powerhouses felt a suffocating pressure in his chest.
Marco, standing nearby, frowned. A dreadful premonition began rising from the depths of his heart.
"Tiana... are you saying they’re doing this on purpose?"
Tiana nodded.
"No matter how many reinforcements the Empire sends, they always keep their numbers just above ours."
Her gaze deepened.
"Think about it. Why would they do that?"
Marco’s face changed drastically.
"They’re putting pressure on us... while still letting us see a chance to hold the line..."
His voice turned hoarse.
"They want us to keep asking the Empire for reinforcements."
"Exactly. If nothing unexpected happens, their goal is to drain the Empire’s supply of legendary-grade powerhouses."
Tiana picked up the thread, a chill creeping into her tone.
"To be precise, they want to drain the Watchers guarding the Abyss Rift."
Hiss—!
Every human powerhouse present sucked in a sharp breath.

At last, one layer of the barrier shattered under the unending bombardment.
The Sixfold Host erupted in thunderous cheers.
"Excellent!
The humans are finally running short on resources!"
"Roar, roar, roar—crush those insects up there!"
"May the Elven God bless us!"
"Victory is ours!"
That shattered barrier was quickly filled in by a fresh new layer of light rising from behind it.
But the blood-maddened warriors of the Sixfold Host only grew more excited.
A thousand miles beyond Winterhold.
Another war was unfolding in a land shrouded by a bizarre and terrifying force.
Across a thousand-mile radius, space itself twisted and warped.
Mist swirled everywhere, as though someone had torn open a crack to another world upon this land.
Dozens of figures were crossing and clashing within this Godscar, every collision unleashing enough force to destroy a city.
The human side had only a little over ten legendary-grade powerhouses.
Opposing them, the Sixfold Host had more than twenty.
The numerical gap was only barely offset by the humans’ perfect coordination and tacit teamwork.
Barely.
Boom—!
A violent blast of power forced an old man on the human side back several steps.
Montague, the peak legendary-grade beastfolk expert, withdrew his fist, swept his gaze across the field, and suddenly shouted:
"Stop!"
At his command, the legendary-grade experts of the six races immediately disengaged from battle and gathered around him with practiced precision.
Montague cast a cold glance at the human powerhouses opposite him, the corner of his mouth curling into a disdainful sneer.
"We’ll spare your miserable lives for today.
Retreat!"
Before the echo of his voice had even faded, more than twenty figures withdrew like a receding tide, vanishing over the horizon in the blink of an eye.
The human powerhouses stared in the direction they had gone, their expressions grave.
"This isn’t normal."
A weak voice came from the crowd.
The priest Tiana leaned against a broken stone pillar, her face pale as paper, but a sharp light still burned in her eyes.
"Haven’t any of you noticed?"
Though her voice was weak, each word came through with complete clarity.
"Every time the balance of the situation starts to tip like this, they withdraw on their own."
"Fuck—these damned non-human races.
Do they really think our human race is easy prey?"
One of the powerhouses felt a suffocating pressure in his chest.
Marco, standing nearby, frowned.
A dreadful premonition began rising from the depths of his heart.
"Tiana... are you saying they’re doing this on purpose?"
Tiana nodded.
"No matter how many reinforcements the Empire sends, they always keep their numbers just above ours."
Her gaze deepened.
"Think about it.
Why would they do that?"
Marco’s face changed drastically.
"They’re putting pressure on us... while still letting us see a chance to hold the line..."
His voice turned hoarse.
"They want us to keep asking the Empire for reinforcements."
"Exactly.
If nothing unexpected happens, their goal is to drain the Empire’s supply of legendary-grade powerhouses."
Tiana picked up the thread, a chill creeping into her tone.
"To be precise, they want to drain the Watchers guarding the Abyss Rift."
Hiss—!
Every human powerhouse present sucked in a sharp breath.

chapters.title: Chapter 105 -105-The Shadow Council’s Conspiracy!
paragraphs: Very soon, the human powerhouses exchanged uneasy glances, their brows tightly furrowed.
At the same time, the same name surfaced in all of their minds:
The Shadow Council!
A scheme of this scale, a hand so skilled at using the entire continent as a chessboard—who else could it be but that organization made up of human traitors?
What a vicious plot!
On one side, they were using the Sixfold Host to pressure Winterhold, forcing the Empire to keep sending reinforcements north.
And where could those reinforcements come from?
Only from the Watchers stationed at the Abyss Rift.
Once the defenses at the Abyss Rift were weakened to a certain point, that would be the day the shadowkin broke free of their seal!
When that time came, the Empire would face shadowkin invasion from within and non-human armies besieging it from without.
Internal strife and external threat, attacking from both sides—the human race would be plunged into utter ruin!
This was a naked, unavoidable stratagem.
The Shadow Council was using the entire continent as its chessboard, with the shadowkin and the six races as its pieces in a grand game against the Human Empire.
And this time, humanity had been forced into a corner with no way out.
Marco’s expression shifted several times. After a long while, he finally forced a sentence out through clenched teeth.
"We can’t just sit here and wait to die. We have to come up with a countermeasure."
The human powerhouses present nodded in silence, every face heavy with grim resolve.
Inside the main camp of the Sixfold Host, Montague led the other non-human experts back into the command tent.
Candlelight flickered within, casting the shadow of a gaunt figure onto the beast-hide drapes.
It was an old man with a full head of silver hair. His face looked like dried tree bark, the wrinkles on it seeming to hide countless conspiracies.
He was dressed almost exactly like Harland had been—black robes embroidered with dark red runes, every line resembling dried blood.
Only one thing was different.
He wore no mask.
That deeply wrinkled face was laid bare in the candlelight, with nothing to conceal it.
"Lord Iris!"
"Greetings, Lord Iris!"
The non-human experts immediately bowed when they saw the old man, their voices filled with unconcealed reverence.
Iris!
The name with the highest bounty on the Empire’s wanted list.
The mentor of the fallen mage Harland, and a peak legendary-grade powerhouse of the dark magic lineage.
His name had hung on the wanted list for a full three hundred years, and not once had anyone ever been able to so much as touch the hem of his robe.
Iris gave a slight nod, expressionless. His aged voice rasped like sandpaper grinding together.
"You have all worked hard these past days."
His withered fingers tapped lightly against the table, producing a steady, muffled rhythm.
"Tomorrow, the twenty legendary-grade powerhouses sent by the Shadow Council will arrive."
Montague’s pupils contracted sharply at those words, then an uncontrollable surge of delight rose in his eyes.
Every non-human expert in the tent revealed the same expression.
Twenty legendary-grade powerhouses, added to their current twenty-five, would make forty-five in total!
If forty-five legendary-grade experts struck at once, what could a mere Winterhold possibly use to stop them?
Montague straightened abruptly, barely suppressing the excitement in his voice.
"Lord Iris, with the Shadow Council’s full support, we will definitely breach Winterhold in one stroke tomorrow!"
A cold curve tugged at the corner of Iris’s mouth.
"If the Empire does not send reinforcements, then we will simply take the northern frontier in one sweep."
"And if they pull the Watchers away from the Abyss Rift..."
A sharp light flashed through his cloudy old eyes.
"Then we let the shadowkin break their seal and pour out from the south."
He slowly rose to his feet, his gaunt shadow drawn long by the candlelight.
"The Empire wants both to hold the north... and to suppress the shadowkin..."
His voice was calm as still water, yet every non-human expert present felt a chill seep into their bones.
"How could there be such a good thing in this world?"
"If they cannot bear to abandon either side, then they are doomed to lose everything!"
South, Ariahold.
The offensive of the human legions, numbering in the tens of millions, crashed against the dark elves’ final line of defense like an enraged tide, wave after wave.

The elves’ rain of arrows was certainly deadly, each shaft capable of claiming a life with perfect precision, but under the overwhelming storm of suppressive fire, their resistance seemed pitifully weak.
Boom—!
With an earth-shaking explosion, Ariahold’s walls finally collapsed under the relentless bombardment.
Broken stone flew everywhere, smoke and dust filled the air, and ancient elven runes turned to ash in the flames.
"Whoa, whoa, whoa... the city’s fallen! Elven Goddess, here I come!"
"Gotta say, these elves really hurt when they fight, but... painful and enjoyable at the same time..."
"Can’t help it. Who told these elves to fight with such absurdly beautiful faces? It’s honestly hard to hate them!"
"Cut the crap and attack! Glory belongs to humanity!"
"Kill—!"
Countless human warriors surged through the breach in the wall like a flood bursting through a broken dam.
Seen from high above, a tide of steel was swallowing the entire city with unstoppable force.
The fall of Ariahold was already set in stone!
Not far from the battlefield, inside the Godscar.
Golden sword-light and violet lightning wove together into a net of death.
Aliris held the Sword of Roses, its blade flowing with brilliant purple radiance.
Every slash she delivered carried enough force to split the earth, crashing down again and again upon the immobilized elven legendary-grade expert.
And above that elven expert’s head, tens of thousands of thunder-serpents were striking down without pause.
Each thunder-serpent carried more than seventy million damage, tearing through his defenses like merciless heavenly punishment.
The last remnant of Immortal Singularity within the elf’s body was rapidly draining away amid the lightning.
Only five seconds!
The moment the final trace of Immortal Singularity was exhausted, his body was reduced to ash in the lightning before he could even let out a scream.
[Ding! You have slain the elven legendary-grade powerhouse "Eric"! EXP +82 billion! Gold coins +1.5 billion!]
[Obtained "Blade of Night (Legendary-Grade)" ×1!]
[Obtained "Darkmoon Hunter Armor (Legendary-Grade)" ×1!]
[Obtained "Lower Divinity Fragment (Legendary-Grade)" ×1!]
Daniel’s expression did not change.
Ariahold’s guardian had been only an early legendary-grade expert. It was perfectly normal for him to drop a Lower Divinity Fragment.
He turned his gaze toward another battlefield not far away.
Carodion was fighting another elven legendary-grade expert, his golden sword-light pouring down like a raging storm and forcing the enemy back step by step.
But Carodion was clearly holding back.
He still remembered Daniel’s order—the final blow had to be left for him.
Daniel activated God Speed, and his figure instantly appeared in the middle of that battlefield.
[Wind’s Embrace]!
Invisible wind-force rushed in from all directions, binding the struggling elven legendary-grade expert tightly in place.
[Serpent’s Thundercell]!
Dark clouds gathered in an instant, and tens of thousands of thunder-serpents came crashing down once again.
A few seconds later—
[Ding! You have slain the elven legendary-grade powerhouse "Erison"! EXP +75 billion! Gold coins +1.3 billion!]
[Obtained "Brush-Hide Belt (Legendary-Grade)" ×1!]
[Obtained "Flying Leaf Boots (Legendary-Grade)" ×1!]
[Obtained "Lower Divinity Fragment (Legendary-Grade)" ×1!]
Daniel frowned slightly.
Another Lower Divinity Fragment.
But it did not matter.
Whether intermediate or lower, they were all the same in his eyes.
Once the players grew stronger in the future, these fragments could also be used to cultivate the elite forces under his command.

chapters.title: Chapter 106 -106-Aliris Advances to Legendary Grade
paragraphs: Daniel opened his inventory and took out the six legendary-grade items gained from this battle.
"Aliris."
He called her over.
Aliris sheathed her sword and walked up, the aura of fierce combat still clinging to her.
She dropped to one knee. Golden blood from the elven powerhouse still stained her silver-white light armor.
"My lord duke."
Daniel held the six legendary-grade items out to her.
"These are yours."
Aliris snapped her head up, disbelief filling her pale golden eyes.
Her lips parted, but it took her a long moment to find her voice again.
"Thank you for your reward, my lord! Aliris is willing to brave fire and water for you—to die ten thousand deaths without regret!"
Daniel smiled.
Aliris’s loyalty to him had already reached the level of life-and-death devotion.
Strengthening her was the same as strengthening himself.
He took another item from his inventory—a crystal radiating seven-colored light—and handed it to her.
"You should have enough accumulated strength by now to break through to legendary-grade, shouldn’t you?"
Aliris accepted the [Star-Tier Stone (Legendary-Grade)]. Feeling the vast power contained within it, a confident gleam flashed in her eyes.
"I am completely certain!"
Daniel nodded.
Aliris stored the six legendary-grade items away, drew a deep breath, and crushed the crystal in her hand.
A pillar of golden light descended from the heavens, piercing through the clouds and enveloping her entire body.
The light was blazing and sacred, as though some ancient god were gazing down upon her.
Within the beam, Aliris slowly rose into the air. Her silver-white light armor shattered into fragments within the golden radiance, replaced by a new suit of armor flowing with golden runes.
The human powerhouses around her stared at the sight and collectively sucked in a sharp breath.
"Wait... th-that’s the sign of advancing to legendary-grade!"
"As expected, war is the cruelest field of flesh and blood—but also the finest whetstone for tempering the strong!"
The players, meanwhile, stared blankly up at the pillar of light that connected heaven and earth.
"By the gods... that light pillar is way too flashy. Is Faustus ascending to godhood?"
"If that were the case, you’d hear an announcement first!"
"What did Faustus do this time? I just took a look with Hawk Eye—it seemed like that female NPC is leveling up?"

"Epic-grade promotion? No, that has to be an advancement to legendary-grade. Otherwise there’s no way it would have this kind of effect. But this is insane! Even Faustus’s captain of the guard is legendary-grade now?"
"So this is what you get for following a big shot? I want to be an NPC too..."
[Ding! The powerhouse under your command, "Aliris (Legendary-Grade)," has successfully advanced to "Legendary-Grade (Early Stage)"!]
The golden light faded, and Aliris slowly descended from the sky.
Her aura was now completely different from before. Those pale golden eyes had become deeper and more profound, and a faint divine radiance seemed to flow around her body.
Daniel cast a detection spell.
[Aliris · LV100 · Legendary-Grade (Early Stage)]
The corner of his mouth lifted slightly.
This was now the second legendary-grade follower at his side!
At that very moment, a world announcement rang out across the entire world of Stellar.
[Server-Wide Announcement!!!]

[Congratulations to player "Faustus" for conquering the elven main city "Ariahold"! Rewards: Contribution Points +100,000! Gold coins +100,000! Special Troop Class Awakening Scroll ×10! NPC Population +100,000! Achievement Earned: "Territory Pioneer"!]
The announcement sounded three times in succession, golden text flashing before every player’s eyes.
The World Channel exploded instantly.
"Faustus has taken another city!"
"By the gods, that makes the third non-human main city, doesn’t it? Beastfolk, dwarves, elves... Faustus has cleaned up all three races!"
"@Faustus, when are you opening teleport permissions, big bro? Don’t misunderstand—I just want to appreciate the architecture of the elven race."
"Hahaha, everyone knows what you’re really thinking. I’m on-site right now, and let me just say this bluntly: if you came here, you’d just be an ugly freak!"
"Damn it, you’re not any better!"
"So what? I’m guarding a bunch of elves right now!"
"Pfft! Go die!"
[Ding! Contribution Points +200,000! Gold coins +300,000! Achievement completed: "Expand the Frontier"!]
[Ding! NPC Population +10,000,000! Special Troop Class Awakening Scroll ×200!]
Listening to the system notifications in his ear, Daniel’s lips curved faintly upward.
The series of rewards left him deeply satisfied.
That much NPC population would be enough to let him maintain overwhelming numerical superiority throughout his expansion.
And the Special Troop Class Awakening Scrolls meant he could upgrade the powerful warriors in his legions into elite troop classes.
Yet before the smile could fully fade from his face, three blood-red announcements stabbed into every heart like three crimson blades.
[Emergency Announcement for World Zone 616: Tiana, Deputy Legion Commander of Winterhold and legendary-grade powerhouse, has fallen in battle!]
[Emergency Announcement for World Zone 616: Cole, Deputy Legion Commander of Winterhold and legendary-grade powerhouse, has fallen in battle!]
[Emergency Announcement for World Zone 616: Upton, Deputy Chief of Staff of Winterhold and legendary-grade powerhouse, has fallen in battle!]
The World Channel fell into instant silence.
Then came a flood of questions.
"By the gods... what happened?!"
"Three legendary-grade powerhouses all died at once? What the hell happened at Winterhold?!"
"Oh my god, this game’s background setting is way too immersive. I instantly got pulled into this whole Empire-on-the-brink atmosphere!"
"Yeah, if this keeps going... are we humans going to lose?!"
"Hahaha, who cares? If the NPCs don’t make way, how are we players supposed to rise?"
"Exactly. If the devs want to keep players around, they have to focus on players. These NPCs are just background props..."
"So where’s the game’s official website?"
Unlike the heated discussion among the players in the World Channel, the smile on Daniel’s face vanished at once.
NPCs?
Those were living, breathing lives!
Three legendary-grade powerhouses had fallen at the same time. The brutality of the war in the north far exceeded his imagination!
Winterhold was likely already on the verge of collapse.
Once the fortress fell, the nearly trillion-strong Sixfold Host would pour into the Empire’s heartland like a tidal wave.
And when that happened, what kind of catastrophe would the Empire’s people in the north face?
Homes destroyed. Families torn apart. Wives and children separated from their loved ones...
He had seen such scenes far too many times.
Daniel took a deep breath and forcibly suppressed the urge to rush north immediately.
That was a battlefield for legendary-grade powerhouses.
With dozens of legendary-grade experts fighting there, even lower- and mid-tier legendary-grade combatants could do little more than barely protect themselves.
With his current strength, even if he went, he would not be able to change the tide.
Rather than throwing his life away, it was better to continue pinning down the strength of the non-human races behind enemy lines.
Every non-human main city he captured was one more share of pressure taken off the northern front.
But for the situation in the north to have deteriorated this far...
It was deeply worrying.
In the end, it all came down to one thing:
The Empire was still not strong enough.

Gold coins +300,000!
Achievement completed: "Expand the Frontier"!]
[Ding!
NPC Population +10,000,000!
Special Troop Class Awakening Scroll ×200!]
Listening to the system notifications in his ear, Daniel’s lips curved faintly upward.
The series of rewards left him deeply satisfied.
That much NPC population would be enough to let him maintain overwhelming numerical superiority throughout his expansion.
And the Special Troop Class Awakening Scrolls meant he could upgrade the powerful warriors in his legions into elite troop classes.
Yet before the smile could fully fade from his face, three blood-red announcements stabbed into every heart like three crimson blades.
[Emergency Announcement for World Zone 616: Tiana, Deputy Legion Commander of Winterhold and legendary-grade powerhouse, has fallen in battle!]
[Emergency Announcement for World Zone 616: Cole, Deputy Legion Commander of Winterhold and legendary-grade powerhouse, has fallen in battle!]
[Emergency Announcement for World Zone 616: Upton, Deputy Chief of Staff of Winterhold and legendary-grade powerhouse, has fallen in battle!]
The World Channel fell into instant silence.
Then came a flood of questions.
"By the gods... what happened?!"
"Three legendary-grade powerhouses all died at once?
What the hell happened at Winterhold?!"
"Oh my god, this game’s background setting is way too immersive.
I instantly got pulled into this whole Empire-on-the-brink atmosphere!"
"Yeah, if this keeps going... are we humans going to lose?!"
"Hahaha, who cares?
If the NPCs don’t make way, how are we players supposed to rise?"
"Exactly.
If the devs want to keep players around, they have to focus on players.
These NPCs are just background props..."
"So where’s the game’s official website?"
Unlike the heated discussion among the players in the World Channel, the smile on Daniel’s face vanished at once.
NPCs?
Those were living, breathing lives!
Three legendary-grade powerhouses had fallen at the same time.
The brutality of the war in the north far exceeded his imagination!
Winterhold was likely already on the verge of collapse.
Once the fortress fell, the nearly trillion-strong Sixfold Host would pour into the Empire’s heartland like a tidal wave.
And when that happened, what kind of catastrophe would the Empire’s people in the north face?
Homes destroyed.
Families torn apart.
Wives and children separated from their loved ones...
He had seen such scenes far too many times.
Daniel took a deep breath and forcibly suppressed the urge to rush north immediately.
That was a battlefield for legendary-grade powerhouses.
With dozens of legendary-grade experts fighting there, even lower- and mid-tier legendary-grade combatants could do little more than barely protect themselves.
With his current strength, even if he went, he would not be able to change the tide.
Rather than throwing his life away, it was better to continue pinning down the strength of the non-human races behind enemy lines.
Every non-human main city he captured was one more share of pressure taken off the northern front.
But for the situation in the north to have deteriorated this far...
It was deeply worrying.
In the end, it all came down to one thing:
The Empire was still not strong enough.

chapters.title: Chapter 107 -107-Abyssal Upheaval, the Empire on the Brink
paragraphs: At first, the Empire’s upper echelon had shown almost no vigilance toward the intensity of this war.
In their eyes, this was nothing more than another round of dissatisfaction from the six non-human races—an alliance formed to pressure humanity into giving them concessions.
One against six, that was all.
The advantage is ours!
But once the war truly began, the Empire’s top-tier strength immediately showed cracks.
The Empire did have quite a few legendary-grade powerhouses. If they were all mobilized, they could absolutely beat the six races into dust.
But the problem was that the overwhelming majority of those legendary-grade experts bore the duty of watching over the Abyss Rift. They simply could not leave their posts!
Those idiots in high office had definitely counted every single legendary-grade powerhouse into the Empire’s combat roster!
A pack of fools who only liked looking at paper data!
Daniel glanced at his wealth value.
"I have to revive them as soon as possible... to fill the gap in humanity’s battle strength."
He took out the [Banner of Valor]. The star embroidered on the banner gave off a faint glow in the dusk.
[Prompt: Spend 3 trillion gold coins to condense the remnant souls of the three fallen human legendary-grade powerhouses?]
"Yes."
Daniel did not hesitate in the slightest.

[Prompt: Incomplete divine souls successfully condensed! Current stored remnant souls: "Tiana (Legendary-Grade, Mid Stage)," "Cole (Legendary-Grade, Early Stage)," "Upton (Legendary-Grade, Early Stage)"!]
He drew a deep breath and continued.
[Prompt: Spend 3 trillion gold coins to convert the remnant souls of the three powerhouses into relics?]
"Yes."
[Prompt: Remnant soul conversion complete!]
Daniel took three relics out of his inventory.
[Tiana’s Relic (Legendary-Grade, Mid Stage)]
[Cole’s Relic (Legendary-Grade, Early Stage)]
[Upton’s Relic (Legendary-Grade, Early Stage)]
Each relic radiated a faint golden glow—the imprint of the obsession those powerhouses had carried in life.
He activated the forbidden spell [Seraphic Revival], placing the three relics one by one into the light.
Once revived, these powerhouses would lose their memories from life and become his followers.
But serving him was the same as serving humanity. There was nothing wrong with that.
[Prompt: Spend 3 trillion gold coins to revive the three human powerhouses?]
"Yes."
[Ding! Successfully revived three human powerhouses!]
Three faint phantoms appeared out of thin air above the altar, gradually solidifying.
When the golden light faded, the three armored powerhouses opened their eyes at the same time and dropped to one knee.
"Good day, my lord!"
Daniel nodded, finally feeling relieved.
Ariahold, Lord’s Manor.
Daniel sat in the seat that had once belonged to the elven guardian, flipping through the war settlement report in his hand.
The system notifications kept sounding at his ear.
[Ding! Obtained "Manastone (Blackgold-Grade)" ×5!]
[Ding! Obtained "Gold Mine (Platinum-Grade)" ×1!]
[Ding! Gold coins +253 billion!]
His gaze fell on the casualty statistics.
The human losses remained extremely low.
And the elven casualties were also far smaller than he had expected.
Daniel was not surprised.
When the army had stormed into the city, many of the elven commanders had voluntarily surrendered to the human legions.
Of course, they had also listed a long string of conditions: treat prisoners well, do not loot civilians, do not destroy the city or the natural environment...
To Daniel, those conditions were nothing much.
Preserving the elven population for his own use was what mattered most.
So long as it did not touch his bottom line, he readily accepted their surrender.
In this battle, more than three million elven warriors and over ten million civilians had been taken prisoner.
After seeing firsthand how ferocious the beastfolk were, Daniel found himself somewhat more interested in the elves.
Perhaps in the future, he could draw some elites from among these elven prisoners and form an elven archer legion.
But for now...
They could go mine first.
Once they had tasted the bitterness of working the mines, they would be far more willing to accept the benefits Daniel later tossed their way.
Daniel withdrew his thoughts and turned his gaze back to the top of the report.
"Manastone..."
His eyes shifted slightly.
When gold coins began to depreciate, mana coins naturally emerged.
It took one hundred gold coins to exchange for a single mana coin, and that exchange rate was recognized by the system itself.
That meant the value of Manastone went far beyond its face worth.
Once the game merged with reality, all kinds of magitech powered by mana would erupt into existence.
Mana cannons, mana wings, mana armor, mana machinery...
They would completely transform the face of the real world!
In short, this was an enormous fortune!
Daniel closed the report and opened the city management interface.
Polaris City, Everfrost, Ariahold, and Ironforge...
The cities under Daniel’s command covered more than ten thousand square kilometers.
Under him were 14.5 million NPC troops and more than 60 million player troops.
Among his legendary-grade powerhouses were the peak-stage expert Carodion, the mid-stage expert Tiana, and the early-stage experts Aliris, Cole, and Upton.
The civilian population under his rule totaled more than 300 million, plus tens of millions of beastfolk, dwarven, and elven military and civilian prisoners.
In the world of Stellar, that was already a force no one could ignore!
Leaning back in his chair, Daniel gazed north through the window lattice.
Once he swept away all the non-human forces, he would forcibly open the World Gate and proactively launch a world war!
The humiliations he had suffered in his previous lives—he would settle them one by one.
Just as he was thinking, a blood-red world announcement suddenly exploded across the sky.
[Emergency Server-Wide Announcement!!!]
[The "Nine-Star Abyss Rift" in Galehold territory has been unsealed! A shadowkin army is about to invade!]
[The "Seven-Star Abyss Rift" in Skyhold territory has been unsealed! A shadowkin army is about to invade!]
[The "Five-Star Abyss Rift" in Luminara territory has been unsealed! A shadowkin army is about to invade!]

[The Abyss is in upheaval, and the shadowkin are invading! The entire world will face the threat of the shadowkin! The flames of war are about to sweep across the land—players, prepare yourselves to confront the abyssal shadowkin!]
Daniel shot to his feet.
The plot had changed again!
A Nine-Star Abyss Rift!
That meant nine legendary-grade powerhouses, among whom there would definitely be peak-stage and even transcendent existences!
The northern fortress was already under pressure from billions of non-human troops, and now the Abyss Rifts inside the Empire had broken their seals at this exact moment...
This had clearly been planned for a very long time!
The fools in the Empire’s upper ranks were probably regretting it so badly their guts had turned green.
Sure enough, another announcement followed immediately after.
[Imperial Edict]
"To the citizens of the Empire!

The northern fortress trembles beneath the iron hoofbeats of the non-human invaders. At the same time, the armies of the shadowkin awaken from the darkness—the hour of reckoning has arrived, and the Empire stands on the brink of destruction.
In this darkest hour, I do not speak to you from a throne with commands, but with the heartbeat of this blood-soaked land.
Let every hand that can wield a sword, every body that can bear armor, every soul that can ride to war hasten toward the frontier and forge yourselves into the wall that will defend our homeland!
This battle is not for glory, nor for conquest, but for the soil beneath our feet.
May the Empire endure! May humanity endure forever!"
[Ding! Do you accept the main version quest "The Empire on the Brink"?]

chapters.title: Chapter 108 -108-Returning the Favor — Slaughtering Our Way into the Abyss
paragraphs: Daniel accepted without the slightest hesitation.
[Prompt: You have accepted the mission! The mission difficulty will be automatically adjusted according to your title and strength!]
He opened the quest log.
[The Empire on the Brink] (Duke Tier)
Quest Difficulty: Legendary-Grade
Objectives:
Repel and crush the invasion of the shadowkin Repel and crush the invasion of the Sixfold Host
Quest Description:

Winterhold is engulfed in endless warfire, its commanding generals falling one after another. The Empire has been forced to redeploy the Rift Watchers northward as reinforcements, leaving the Rift seals weakened. Seizing the opportunity, the Shadow Council has broken the seals, and countless shadowkin are pouring out of the Abyss. At the same time, deep within the Demon Abyss, the shadowkin overlord has already united the demon domain. With the non-human races pressing in from without and the shadowkin breaking free from within, the Human Empire now faces enemies on both fronts. The torch of civilization flickers in the wind—whether it endures or is extinguished will be decided today!
Quest Duration: Long-term
Quest Rewards: Imperial Morale, Human Merit, merit points / gold coins / Contribution Points, Divinity Fragments, achievements, titles, noble rank, special items, World Key...
Daniel closed the quest log.
His gaze lingered on the words World Key for a moment before moving away.
This quest offered an extremely high degree of freedom, yet the rewards were anything but stingy.
Now that the non-human races and the shadowkin were invading at the same time, with the Shadow Council lurking in the dark and waiting for its chance, every move had to be made with caution.
He closed the mission panel and summoned all the powerhouses under his command.
Inside the council hall, Carodion, Tiana, Aliris, Cole, and Upton stood in a straight line, every face solemn as iron.
Daniel swept his gaze over them and spoke directly.
"All of you will follow me to the Abyss Rift and suppress the shadowkin!"
At once, battle intent flared in the eyes of every powerhouse present.
"We are willing to brave fire and water for you, my lord!"
Luminara, Five-Star Abyss Rift.
Six figures dove out of the clouds and landed steadily on the open ground before the entrance to the Abyss Rift.
Daniel gazed at the crack spilling out endless black mist and frowned slightly.
The surrounding area was deathly silent. Not even the chirping of insects could be heard. This calm was far too abnormal.
But he knew it was only a surface illusion.
Inside the Abyss Rift, it was probably already a landscape of mountains of corpses and seas of blood.
Scattered around the entrance were large numbers of shadowkin corpses. Some had been cut in two, some burned into charcoal, and some frozen into ice statues.
Whoever had struck had done so cleanly and decisively, without the slightest bit of wasted movement.
Daniel withdrew his gaze and strode toward the entrance of the Abyss Rift.
"Move in."
Before the words had even fully fallen, he had already rushed into the black mist.
Carodion and the others followed close behind. In the blink of an eye, all six figures were swallowed by darkness.
On a distant tower, a golden figure watched all of this in silence, making no move to stop them.
He was the Watcher of this Abyss Rift.
The shadowkin corpses at the entrance had been slain by his hand.
He had only one duty—to suppress any shadowkin that attempted to break through the seal.
As for people going in?
That was none of his business, and not within his power to stop.
Inside the Abyss Rift.
Before them stretched a dark crimson wasteland.
Several violet crescent moons floated in the sky, casting a strange and ghostly glow across the land.
In the distance, a vast shadowkin army was assembling, a black mass so dense it stretched beyond sight.
"Carodion."
Daniel spoke in a deep voice.
Carodion gave a slight nod.
"Understood."
He led Tiana, Aliris, and the others, transforming into five streaks of light as they sped toward the rear of the shadowkin army.
There, several terrifying auras could be sensed.
Legendary-grade powerhouses!
Daniel unfurled the Eternal Black King, his blackgold-colored wings tracing a dazzling arc beneath the broken moons.
In mere moments, he was already above the shadowkin army.
"Human?!"
"You insects have a lot of nerve, daring to venture deep into shadowkin territory!"
"Damned humans! The debt from back then—when you colluded with the god race—hasn’t been settled yet. Today, we’ll start by taking your lives!"
Countless shadowkin warriors looked up, their crimson eyes locked firmly on the figure in the sky.
Arrows, magic, and curses poured toward him like a storm.
Daniel’s expression remained unchanged.
[Starveil]!
A pale golden starlight shield condensed around him. Attacks powerful enough to tear through city walls struck it and produced nothing more than tiny ripples.
He raised Stellar Wrath.
[Arrowstorm]!
[Shattering Comet]!
[Serpent’s Thundercell]!
The bowstring trembled as three skills erupted at once.
Countless arrows transformed into a rain of fire and lightning serpents, crashing down like an apocalyptic disaster.
Crimson critical-hit damage numbers exploded throughout the shadowkin army like flowers of death in full bloom.
Even legendary-grade shadowkin commanders were like paper in front of him. As for epic-grade warriors, they did not even have time to scream before turning to ash.
With one volley, hundreds of thousands of shadowkin were annihilated!
Two volleys. Three volleys...
In just a few short minutes, this shadowkin legion of several million was already on the verge of collapse.
The surviving shadowkin soldiers stared at that blackgold-colored figure in the sky, their eyes filled with terror.
"That’s a legendary-grade powerhouse?"
"Impossible... he doesn’t have a legendary-grade aura!"
"But this is absurd! Why is he this strong?!"
"Find a way to kill him!"
Daniel gave them no chance.
The arrow rain did not stop. The lightning did not cease.
Tens of thousands of lightning serpents roamed across the battlefield, leaving utter desolation in their wake.
Ten minutes later, the entire shadowkin legion had been wiped out!
[Ding! Gold coins +250,000! EXP +1.6 billion!]
Daniel spread his wings and flew toward the distorted region of space in the distance.
Godscar.
Five terrifying auras were colliding madly within this torn-apart region of space.
Every clash released power enough to flatten mountains. The earth trembled, and the sky burned.
Carodion was locked in combat with the shadowkin leader.
Golden sword light and dark crimson demonic flames intertwined into a net of death, the surrounding air twisting from the heat.

On the other four battlefields, Tiana, Aliris, Cole, and Upton were fighting the remaining four legendary-grade shadowkin. Both sides were evenly matched, and there was no clear winner for the moment.
Just then, Daniel’s figure appeared at the edge of the battlefield.
The shadowkin leader, Regroth, noticed the uninvited guest immediately.
While parrying Carodion’s assault, he glanced sidelong at the human archer and pulled his lips into a scornful smile.
"Has humanity run out of people? They actually sent an ant here to die?"
Daniel remained expressionless and quietly cast a detection spell.
[Shadowkin Leader · Regroth (Legendary-Grade · High Stage)]
Level: 95
Defense: 8,800,000
Skills: Abyss Descends, Demonflame Slash, Whispering Curse, Shadow Guard, Abyssal Demonic Power...
Indestructible Substance: Regroth points
Description: The ruler of the Five-Star Abyss Rift, a high-stage legendary-grade shadowkin powerhouse, and one of the thirty-six Grand Lords serving under the Shadowkin Overlord!
