chapters.title: Chapter 116 -116-Permafrost Prison, Ring of Void
paragraphs: The two world announcements crashed down one after another like thunderbolts.
In an instant, the entire Multiversal World Channel exploded into chaos.
"What the hell?! We players from other world regions contributed to the defense against the shadowkin invasion too. Why does only World Region No. 616 get double EXP? How is that fair?!"
"Protest! We players from other regions don’t want anything else—just fair treatment!"
"Holy shit, I didn’t expect the system itself to be this biased! Was this game developed by players from World Region No. 616 or what?!"
But over in World Region No. 616, the public channel was nothing but celebration.
"Thanks to the great Faustus for winning us double EXP! This is insane!"
"@Faustus, Guildmaster is forever our god!"
"By the gods, I hereby declare that from today onward, Faustus is my idol!"
"Everyone, latest news—Munich Guild has disbanded on the spot! I heard even their guildmaster has already joined Doom Guild!"
"Hahahaha... That’s completely normal. Here’s something you probably don’t know—those financial conglomerates back on Earth are now totally helpless when it comes to this game!"

"The exchange rate between dollars and gold coins has already skyrocketed to 20:1! And even if they have gold coins, they still can’t buy the most core assets in the nine main cities. I heard all those commercial properties have been monopolized by Faustus!"
"What? Faustus is that outrageous?"
"Of course! Otherwise, how could he possibly pull off something as heaven-defying as killing the shadowkin overlord?"
[Ding! You have slain the shadowkin overlord! Luck +100! Charisma +100! Achievement obtained: "Human Watcher"!]
[Achievement rewards obtained:
epic-grade NPC ×10,000!
Exalted-grade NPC ×5,000!
legendary-grade NPC (low-grade) ×10!
The rewards have been automatically delivered to Polaris City.]
Daniel let out a long breath.
At long last, the massive trouble posed by the shadowkin had been dealt with.
Now, all he had to do was crush the Sixfold Host in Winterhold of the North, and this mission would be fully completed.
And this trip to the Abyss Rift had brought him an astonishing harvest.
With the ten newly rewarded legendary-grade NPCs added in, the number of legendary-grade powerhouses under his command had surged to thirty.
Four transcendent, eight high-grade, five mid-grade, and thirteen low-grade.
This force was enough to let him stand against any future version update, and it also gave him the confidence to confront the Shadow Council head-on.
He opened his inventory and began checking his spoils.
Among the items dropped by the shadowkin overlord Baal, the most eye-catching was a skill book glowing with an icy blue radiance.
[Permafrost Prison (SSS-rank Forbidden Art)]
Learning Requirement: Archer / Level 150

Effect: Draw upon the power of absolute frost and transform it into an arrow, creating a realm of eternal ice within a designated area (1000 × 1000 meters). All enemy targets within the domain are forcibly afflicted with [Frozen], [Slowed], and [Icebound]. Enemies inside the domain take damage equal to 200% of the caster’s Attack Power every second.
Duration: Infinite (can be terminated by the caster at any time; consumes 1% MP per second)

Description: A forbidden art said to have been created by an ancient Great Sage Archer, using the heart of a Frost Dragon as its catalyst. Once the arrow is loosed, all lands for ten thousand miles are sealed in ice.
Including [Heavenfall Strike] and [Thunder Abyss], which he had obtained earlier, Daniel had now collected three forbidden arts.
Unfortunately, the learning requirement for forbidden arts was Level 150, so he still could not use them for the time being.
With that thought, he put away the skill book and took out a ring glowing with a soft golden light.
[Ring of Space (legendary-grade)]
Effect: Grants an independent storage space of 300 × 300 slots. Living beings cannot be stored inside.**
Daniel placed the softly glowing ring into the guild warehouse and tapped his fingertip lightly to confirm the sale.
[Ding! You have sold "Ring of Space (legendary-grade)" to Doom Guild for 1 copper coin, triggering Millionfold Boost!]
[The item sold belongs to the special equipment category. Please choose: quality boost / quantity boost!]
"Quality boost!"
[Congratulations! You have obtained 1 gold coin! You have obtained "Ring of Void (supreme-grade)"!]
He took the brand-new ring out of his inventory.
Unlike the previous one, this ring was entirely pitch black. A deep-blue gem was set into its surface, and within that gem, it seemed as though an endless galaxy slowly revolved.
The ring felt almost weightless in his hand. The moment he put it on, an indescribable power spread from his fingertip throughout his entire body.
[Ring of Void (supreme-grade)]

Effect: Grants an independent space of 1000 × 1000 slots. Living beings may be stored inside. Time within the space flows in sync with the outside world, and living creatures inside may survive, rest, and recover from injuries normally.**

Special: The wearer may anchor the entrance to the space at any chosen location and set access permissions. Buildings may be constructed within the space, crops may be planted, and living creatures may be raised there, as though it were a portable world.

Description: Legend says that the ancient God of the Void forged this ring from the Core of the Void to imprison beings that even gods could not truly destroy. Later, the ring passed into mortal hands, and its bearer became the sovereign of that world within.
Daniel stared at the description in silence for a full five seconds.
A portable miniature world!
Converted into real-world area, it was large enough to hold a small castle.
And it could store living beings, grow crops, and raise animals.
He slipped the ring onto his finger. With a single thought, his consciousness instantly sank into that void space.
It was a gray-white world. The ground was smooth as a mirror, and above was an endless expanse of bright white emptiness.
The edges of the space were wrapped in a faint golden wall of light, across which ancient runes flowed.
"A fine treasure."
Daniel withdrew from the space, the corners of his lips curving slightly upward.
With this ring, he could store all thirty legendary-grade powerhouses under his command inside it.
Just imagine it—using a portal to descend upon the main city of an enemy world region, and then releasing thirty legendary-grade powerhouses from the ring in an instant...
The very thought of that scene was enough to make one’s scalp tingle.
Not far away, the human legendary-grade powerhouses had gathered together.
"Carodion... just now, you addressed that young man as ’my lord’?"
an elderly man asked hesitantly.
"You... were truly revived by him?"
Unfortunately, faced with everyone’s questions, Carodion and the others gave no response at all.
"It’s good to see you again..."
Another powerhouse looked at Carodion’s hollow gaze, his voice choking slightly.
"Even though you’ve lost your former memories, at least... you’re still alive."
"Yes. As long as you’re alive, that’s enough."
After finishing his inspection of the spoils, Daniel turned and walked toward that group of legendary-grade powerhouses.
"My lord."
All thirty powerhouses bowed in unison.
Daniel nodded, his gaze sweeping across the other human powerhouses.
"The shadowkin have been destroyed. You may all return."
At that moment, an aged legendary-grade powerhouse stepped forward. After hesitating for a moment, he asked softly,
"My lord... could you tell us what exactly Carodion and the others went through? For the dead to return to life, there must have been some price to pay, no?"

sentences.text: The two world announcements crashed down one after another like thunderbolts.
In an instant, the entire Multiversal World Channel exploded into chaos.
"What the hell?!
We players from other world regions contributed to the defense against the shadowkin invasion too.
Why does only World Region No.
616 get double EXP?
How is that fair?!"
"Protest!
We players from other regions don’t want anything else—just fair treatment!"
"Holy shit, I didn’t expect the system itself to be this biased!
Was this game developed by players from World Region No.
616 or what?!"
But over in World Region No.
616, the public channel was nothing but celebration.
"Thanks to the great Faustus for winning us double EXP!
This is insane!"
"@Faustus, Guildmaster is forever our god!"
"By the gods, I hereby declare that from today onward, Faustus is my idol!"
"Everyone, latest news—Munich Guild has disbanded on the spot!
I heard even their guildmaster has already joined Doom Guild!"
"Hahahaha...
That’s completely normal.
Here’s something you probably don’t know—those financial conglomerates back on Earth are now totally helpless when it comes to this game!"
"The exchange rate between dollars and gold coins has already skyrocketed to 20:1!
And even if they have gold coins, they still can’t buy the most core assets in the nine main cities.
I heard all those commercial properties have been monopolized by Faustus!"
"What?
Faustus is that outrageous?"
"Of course!
Otherwise, how could he possibly pull off something as heaven-defying as killing the shadowkin overlord?"

You have slain the shadowkin overlord!
Luck +100!
Charisma +100!
Achievement obtained: "Human Watcher"!]

epic-grade NPC ×10,000!
Exalted-grade NPC ×5,000!
legendary-grade NPC (low-grade) ×10!
The rewards have been automatically delivered to Polaris City.]
Daniel let out a long breath.
At long last, the massive trouble posed by the shadowkin had been dealt with.
Now, all he had to do was crush the Sixfold Host in Winterhold of the North, and this mission would be fully completed.
And this trip to the Abyss Rift had brought him an astonishing harvest.
With the ten newly rewarded legendary-grade NPCs added in, the number of legendary-grade powerhouses under his command had surged to thirty.
Four transcendent, eight high-grade, five mid-grade, and thirteen low-grade.
This force was enough to let him stand against any future version update, and it also gave him the confidence to confront the Shadow Council head-on.
He opened his inventory and began checking his spoils.
Among the items dropped by the shadowkin overlord Baal, the most eye-catching was a skill book glowing with an icy blue radiance.
[Permafrost Prison (SSS-rank Forbidden Art)]
Learning Requirement: Archer / Level 150
Effect: Draw upon the power of absolute frost and transform it into an arrow, creating a realm of eternal ice within a designated area (1000 × 1000 meters).
All enemy targets within the domain are forcibly afflicted with [Frozen], [Slowed], and [Icebound].
Enemies inside the domain take damage equal to 200% of the caster’s Attack Power every second.
Duration: Infinite (can be terminated by the caster at any time; consumes 1% MP per second)
Description: A forbidden art said to have been created by an ancient Great Sage Archer, using the heart of a Frost Dragon as its catalyst.
Once the arrow is loosed, all lands for ten thousand miles are sealed in ice.

Effect: Grants an independent storage space of 300 × 300 slots.
Living beings cannot be stored inside.**

You have sold "Ring of Space (legendary-grade)" to Doom Guild for 1 copper coin, triggering Millionfold Boost!]

Please choose: quality boost / quantity boost!]
"Quality boost!"
[Congratulations!
You have obtained 1 gold coin!
You have obtained "Ring of Void (supreme-grade)"!]

chapters.title: Chapter 117 -117-Bound for the Battlefield of Winterhold
paragraphs: Daniel’s gaze swept across the surroundings like a blazing torch.
"For the dead to return to life, the price is naturally no small one. As you can already see, they have lost all of their memories."
His voice was calm as still water, yet utterly beyond question.
"As for the rest, I will say no more."
"But you may rest assured—these revived forebears once shed their blood for the human race, and I will never dishonor their reborn bodies."
He had no need to hide anything, nor any need to explain.
With the strength he possessed now, no one could force him to reveal any of his secrets.
The old man fell silent for a moment before finally nodding slowly.
"To be able to return to life is already a heaven-given fortune. Since that is the case... then let us not trouble my lord any further. We should be on our way."
"Mm."
"Bruno, Cole... farewell!"
Dozens of figures lingered with reluctance and sorrow, but in the end, they all turned into streaks of light and disappeared at the edge of the Godscar.
Daniel withdrew his gaze and turned it toward the shadowkin castle in the distance.
There were still tens of millions of shadowkin warriors waiting for him to reap.
He flew above the shadowkin castle and raised Stellar Wrath.
[Arrowstorm].
[Shattering Comet].
[Aetherlance].
[Serpent’s Thundercell].
Four skills erupted at once, transforming into thousands of attacks that poured down like an apocalyptic catastrophe.
[Ding! You have slain a shadowkin overlord! Gold coins +450,000! Obtained "Armor of Envy (legendary-grade)" ×1!]
[Ding! You have slain a shadowkin commander! Gold coins +190,000! Obtained "Demonic Warblade (Exalted-grade)" ×1!]
[Ding! You have slain a shadowkin commander! Gold coins +160,000! Obtained "Demonic Warbracers (Exalted-grade)" ×1!]
System notifications surged in like a tidal wave, and Daniel directly turned off the repeated prompts.
Half an hour later, the shadowkin castle that had stood in the depths of the Abyss Rift for countless millennia had been reduced completely to ruins.
Looking at the scorched wasteland before him, Daniel nodded in satisfaction.
"The shadowkin threat has been resolved. Next..."
He lifted his gaze northward, and a cold gleam flashed in his eyes.
"It’s time to head to the Northern Frontier."
Winterhold, the Great Wall of the North.
"Flatten the human fortress! Use their heads as offerings to our ancestors!"
"In this battle, our Mammoth Tribe will be victorious! Kill!"
"Chirrup-chirrup-chirrup! Charge!"
Endless slaughter had dyed the entire region crimson with blood.
The warriors of the six great non-human races and the human warriors fought each other desperately on a battlefield like a giant meat grinder. Every second, hundreds of lives vanished.
And within the Godscar, the slaughter among legendary-grade powerhouses was still ongoing.
At that moment, a figure appeared at the edge of the Godscar.
It was none other than Daniel.
With the Eternal Black King spread wide, he stood beneath that twisted sky, sizing up the Godscar before him.
This battlefield was actually even grander than the one at the nine-star Abyss Rift, and the spatial fluctuations here were even more violent.
"No wonder the Empire could only spare so few people to suppress the Abyss Rift... so the main force was all tied down here."
He raised a hand and activated the [Ring of Void] in his grasp.
Whoosh, whoosh, whoosh...
Twenty figures appeared out of nowhere—Carodion, Lucian, Tiana...
Twenty legendary-grade powerhouses stood in a single line, each of them radiating a suffocating pressure.

The ten low legendary-grade powerhouses rewarded by the system were all still in Polaris City. On top of that, Daniel had come in a hurry and had not brought them along. Besides, low legendary-grade powerhouses would not have been of much help on the fiercest battlefield anyway.
Daniel looked at the twisted battlefield before him, his voice sharp and commanding.
"Follow me. Drive out the non-human races and clear away every obstacle before humankind."
"We are willing to follow you, my lord!"
All twenty figures answered at once.
Daniel spread his wings and charged into the Godscar first.
The twenty legendary-grade powerhouses followed closely behind, like twenty unsheathed blades stabbing straight into the enemy ranks.
"It’s you, Faustus—!"
Inside the Godscar, an aged roar exploded like thunder.
Daniel turned toward the source of the voice and saw an old man shrouded in dark aura rushing straight at him.
The man was dressed in a black robe. His face was gaunt, and his eyes were filled with venom and killing intent.
Dark mage Iris!
The most heavily wanted figure on the Empire’s bounty list!
"Faustus! You dared kill my student, and now you actually dare come here to throw your life away!"
A flash of black light burst from Iris’s body. He abruptly abandoned the opponent in front of him and appeared near Daniel in an instant.
"Protect my lord!"
Carodion’s reaction was as fast as lightning.
The four transcendent powerhouses moved at the same time, stepping in front of Daniel to intercept Iris’s attack.
Iris froze for a moment.
"What is going on?"
A cold smile curved across Daniel’s lips.
As expected, this old fellow was most likely the mentor of that fallen imperial genius, Hadlan.
But judging from the current situation, it seemed this decrepit old thing had delivered himself to death of his own accord.
"We’ll leave him to them. You go deal with the other non-human races."
He gave the order to the powerhouses beside him.
Very soon, more than a dozen figures turned into streaks of light and shot toward every corner of the battlefield.
Daniel’s gaze returned to Iris.
At that moment, the four transcendent powerhouses were launching a frenzied assault against the dark mage.
Golden sword-light, silver spear shadows, and dark crimson flames intertwined into a net of death, trapping Iris firmly in the center.
Iris’s expression turned ashen.
For the first time, he felt a trace of regret for his earlier impulsiveness.
How could this human youth possibly have so many transcendent powerhouses at his side?
Daniel leisurely cast a Detection spell.
[Iris · transcendent legendary-grade]
Description: A core member of the Shadow Council, the supreme powerhouse of the dark magic lineage, and the highest-bountied existence on the Empire’s wanted list.
After reading the information, Daniel’s smile deepened.
Even Peak Transcendent overlord Baal had struggled when besieged by four powerhouses of the same tier, let alone Iris!
After several minutes of battle, Iris was already at the end of his strength.
"Now!"
Carodion gave a loud shout.
Daniel’s figure instantly appeared before Iris.
[Wind’s Embrace]!
[Serpent’s Thundercell]!
Even Daniel himself was stunned for a moment by those damage numbers approaching eight hundred million.
But he quickly understood why.
His title granted tenfold bonus damage against dark-aligned beings.
And Iris just happened to be dark-aligned.
[Ding! You have slain Shadow Council Leader Boss "Iris"!
Obtained skill book "Shadow Arrow"!
Obtained "High-tier Divinity Fragment" ×1!
Obtained "Heavenscar Pass" ×1!
Obtained "Ascension Stone (legendary-grade)" ×2!]
Daniel’s eyes flickered slightly.
A dark-element skill book—this really was an unexpected delight.
He took out the skill book, which glowed with a dim violet radiance, and chose to learn it without the slightest hesitation.
[Ding! You have successfully mastered the skill "Shadow Arrow (SSS-rank)"!]
[Shadow Arrow (SSS-rank)]
Effect: Inflicts a triple-layered dark curse on a designated target for one minute.
[Dark Abyss]: Causes the target to fall into a coma.
[Dark Illusion]: Directly reduces the target’s maximum HP by 1% and maximum MP by 1%.
[Dark Erosion]: Randomly seals one of the target’s active skills.
Description: A core forbidden art of dark magic. With a single thought, it can cast an opponent into an abyss of eternal damnation. However, beware—light magic can dispel it.
After reading through the skill’s details, Daniel closed the interface.
This was his first curse-type skill.
Three layers of negative effects—each one could be called top-tier.

chapters.title: Chapter 118 -118-Special Players in the Corners of the World
paragraphs: In addition to the skill books, there were also two Ascension Stones.
With that, two more mid-grade powerhouses would soon join his ranks.
His gaze swept across the entirety of Godscar.
Combined, the allied forces of the non-human races and the Shadow Council still had well over a hundred legendary-grade experts, while humanity had originally possessed only a little over sixty.
But with the twenty fresh reinforcements he had brought—twenty of the very best reinforcements, no less—the human side had completely stabilized its position.
A faint smile curved Daniel’s lips.
Next came the harvest.
In a hidden pocket world, several hundred players stood atop the city walls, staring out at the boundless undead army beyond the city.
Skeleton warriors surged forward like a tidal wave. Gold-grade skeleton warriors raised their battle blades high, leading the endless flood of bones.
Rotting corpses, gargoyles, liches, undead knights, hell reapers...
Countless undead creatures were closing in on this solitary city.
And in the skies above, dozens of bone dragons circled overhead.
Their riders gripped pitch-black lances as they tore through the clouds at will, letting out ear-piercing shrieks.
The faces of the hundreds of players had turned deathly pale, their eyes filled with terror.
Charles, a player from World Zone No. 616, clenched his fists tightly and turned to glare at the group of players from other world zones, fury blazing in his eyes.
"Look at the mess you’ve caused!"
His voice trembled with rage.
"All for some stupid quest, and you actually tore open the undead passage! Did any of you even think about the consequences?"

"Yes, this is a game—but our choices can still determine the direction of the entire game. And unless something unexpected happens, the whole of Aetheria is going to be swallowed by these piles of bones!"
"Hmph!"
Averly, a player from World Zone No. 1213, let out a cold sneer.
"What, can’t handle it anymore?"
He folded his arms, his face full of disdain.
"The system’s quest was to open the undead passage. Are we supposed to give up an SSS-grade reward just because of your pathetic little sense of justice? Don’t be naïve."
He paused, his gaze sweeping across every player present.
"We chosen ones all possess hidden talents of S-grade or above. From the very first day the servers opened, we were thrown into this dump and forced to claw our way up step by step."
"With our strength, the moment we return to the main world, we’ll rise to the very top of the player rankings in no time."
The more he spoke, the more excited he became, and a feverish gleam lit up his eyes.
"And when that happens, we can lead all those rookies in the main world and wipe out the undead calamity ourselves. Fame and fortune, both in our hands. Isn’t that perfect?"
Those words deeply resonated with the crowd. Even quite a few players from World Zone No. 616 found themselves secretly agreeing.
"Averly’s right! We’re the chosen ones—the group with the highest talents in the entire game!"
"How could the players in the main world possibly compare to us?"
"Once we get back, they’ll be begging on their knees for us to carry them!"
"Exactly! What’s the point of defending this broken city? Let it fall. That way we can finally head back to the main world."
"I’ve wanted to go there for ages. This place is unbearable—same few faces over and over again. I’m sick of it."
"Once we return to the main world, every one of us will be a god-tier player. We’ll scare the life out of those country bumpkins and show them what real power looks like!"
As Charles listened to the chatter, his expression darkened like storm clouds.
Inwardly, he let out a helpless sigh.
"Charles, you’re taking this way too seriously. It’s just a game—does it really matter that much?"
One of the players from World Zone No. 616 patted him on the shoulder.
"Yeah. It’s just a game. What difference does it make where you play?"
Charles said nothing.
He simply stared at the overwhelming undead army in the distance and tightened his grip on the sword in his hand.
Winterhold, Godscar, in the northern frontier.
Ever since Daniel’s forces had descended upon the battlefield like a thunderclap, the tide of war had begun tilting at an unstoppable speed.
In less than half an hour, humanity’s experts had already driven the coalition army of the non-human races and the Shadow Council into complete despair.
Those legendary-grade non-human experts who had once been so arrogant were now few and far between.
One after another, they fell beneath Daniel’s arrows, dissolving into golden motes of light that scattered through the warped space.
The final survivor was the beastfolk expert, Montague.
His body was drenched in blood, golden blood streaming from dozens of wounds and staining the cracked earth beneath his feet.
His breathing was ragged and labored, every breath accompanied by intense pain.
And yet he remained standing, preserving the last dignity of a warrior amid mountains of corpses and seas of blood.
Then, an endless torrent of skills engulfed him.
A few moments later, Montague coughed up mouthful after mouthful of blood, his body swaying on the verge of collapse.
His eyes swept across the battlefield—
The non-human experts who had once fought alongside him were now nothing more than cold corpses, scattered across every corner of Godscar.
He knew that today, he was doomed.
The great plan of the six races had failed completely.
"No! I refuse to accept this—!"
Montague threw back his head and roared to the heavens, his voice filled with rage and unwillingness.
At that very moment, Daniel’s figure appeared before him.
[Wind’s Embrace]!
Invisible chains of wind surged from the void, binding Montague fast.
Faint golden runes flowed along those chains, each one containing the ancient laws of wind.
[Source of Shadow]!
Three layers of dark curses descended at once. A dark abyss dragged him into unconsciousness, a dark illusion eroded his life force, and a dark seal locked away his final means of resistance.
[Serpent’s Thundercell]!
Tens of thousands of thunder serpents poured down from the sky, violet lightning illuminating the whole of Godscar as brightly as day.
[Ding! You have killed the non-human races leader BOSS "Montague"! Experience +2,000,000,000! Contribution Points +900,000! Gold Coins +1,500,000!]
[Obtained "High-tier Divinity Fragment" ×5!
Obtained "Heavenscar Pass" ×10!
Obtained "Ethereal Shard" ×5!]
The corners of Daniel’s lips lifted slightly.
At last, the final leader of the non-human races had fallen.
Still, Montague’s strength was nowhere near that of the shadowkin overlord Baal, and the loot he dropped could only be considered decent at best.
Daniel put away the spoils and shifted his gaze beyond Godscar.
Out there, tens of millions of non-human troops were still besieging Winterhold.
Daniel shot out of Godscar and rose above the vast army of the non-human races.
He raised his staff, and four skills erupted at once, splitting into more than a hundred attacks that poured down like an apocalyptic natural disaster.
[Arrowstorm].
[Shattering Comet].
[Aetherlance].
[Serpent’s Thundercell].
[Ding! You have killed large numbers of non-human commanders! Gold Coins +2,530,000! Obtained "Berserker Armor (Exalted-grade)" ×1! ...]
[Ding! You have killed large numbers of non-human elites! Gold Coins +1,640,000! Obtained "Bloodbattle Blade (Exalted-grade)" ×1! ...]
[Ding! You have killed large numbers of non-human warriors! Gold Coins +1,160,000! Obtained "Berserker Bracers (Exalted-grade)" ×1! ...]
After several volleys, the vast non-human army that had once blotted out the sky was reduced to a field of corpses and ashes.

sentences.text: In addition to the skill books, there were also two Ascension Stones.
With that, two more mid-grade powerhouses would soon join his ranks.
His gaze swept across the entirety of Godscar.
Combined, the allied forces of the non-human races and the Shadow Council still had well over a hundred legendary-grade experts, while humanity had originally possessed only a little over sixty.
But with the twenty fresh reinforcements he had brought—twenty of the very best reinforcements, no less—the human side had completely stabilized its position.
A faint smile curved Daniel’s lips.
Next came the harvest.
In a hidden pocket world, several hundred players stood atop the city walls, staring out at the boundless undead army beyond the city.
Skeleton warriors surged forward like a tidal wave.
Gold-grade skeleton warriors raised their battle blades high, leading the endless flood of bones.
Rotting corpses, gargoyles, liches, undead knights, hell reapers...
Countless undead creatures were closing in on this solitary city.
And in the skies above, dozens of bone dragons circled overhead.
Their riders gripped pitch-black lances as they tore through the clouds at will, letting out ear-piercing shrieks.
The faces of the hundreds of players had turned deathly pale, their eyes filled with terror.
Charles, a player from World Zone No.
616, clenched his fists tightly and turned to glare at the group of players from other world zones, fury blazing in his eyes.
"Look at the mess you’ve caused!"
His voice trembled with rage.
"All for some stupid quest, and you actually tore open the undead passage!
Did any of you even think about the consequences?"
"Yes, this is a game—but our choices can still determine the direction of the entire game.
And unless something unexpected happens, the whole of Aetheria is going to be swallowed by these piles of bones!"
"Hmph!"
Averly, a player from World Zone No.
1213, let out a cold sneer.
"What, can’t handle it anymore?"
He folded his arms, his face full of disdain.
"The system’s quest was to open the undead passage.
Are we supposed to give up an SSS-grade reward just because of your pathetic little sense of justice?
Don’t be naïve."
He paused, his gaze sweeping across every player present.
"We chosen ones all possess hidden talents of S-grade or above.
From the very first day the servers opened, we were thrown into this dump and forced to claw our way up step by step."
"With our strength, the moment we return to the main world, we’ll rise to the very top of the player rankings in no time."
The more he spoke, the more excited he became, and a feverish gleam lit up his eyes.
"And when that happens, we can lead all those rookies in the main world and wipe out the undead calamity ourselves.
Fame and fortune, both in our hands.
Isn’t that perfect?"
Those words deeply resonated with the crowd.
Even quite a few players from World Zone No.
616 found themselves secretly agreeing.
"Averly’s right!
We’re the chosen ones—the group with the highest talents in the entire game!"
"How could the players in the main world possibly compare to us?"
"Once we get back, they’ll be begging on their knees for us to carry them!"
"Exactly!
What’s the point of defending this broken city?
Let it fall.
That way we can finally head back to the main world."
"I’ve wanted to go there for ages.
This place is unbearable—same few faces over and over again.
I’m sick of it."
"Once we return to the main world, every one of us will be a god-tier player.
We’ll scare the life out of those country bumpkins and show them what real power looks like!"

Inwardly, he let out a helpless sigh.
"Charles, you’re taking this way too seriously.
It’s just a game—does it really matter that much?"
One of the players from World Zone No.
616 patted him on the shoulder.
"Yeah.
It’s just a game.
What difference does it make where you play?"

He simply stared at the overwhelming undead army in the distance and tightened his grip on the sword in his hand.

chapters.title: Chapter 119 -119-Advancement to Grand Duke, Granted Lands to Rule as King
paragraphs: When the very last non-human warrior fell, the long-awaited system notification arrived right on cue.
[Ding! You have completed the quest "Twilight of the Empire"!]
[Ding! You have obtained Gold Coins +2,000,000,000! Contribution Points +2,000,000,000! Merit Points +3,000,000,000! Imperial Morale +600,000! Human Merit +600,000!]
[Obtained "High-tier Divinity Fragment" ×20!
Obtained "Heavenscar Pass (low-grade)" ×20!
Obtained "Ethereal Shard" ×10!
Obtained "Ascension Stone (legendary-grade)" ×5!
Obtained "Key of World (Special Item)"!
Obtained "Phantom Potion (legendary-grade)"!]
Daniel froze for a moment.
The gains from this wave were visibly enormous.
He had now gathered enough High-tier Divinity Fragments.
As long as he reached Level 100, he would be able to fuse a divinity and step into the legendary-grade realm.
The Ascension Stone rewards were equally generous.
These rewards were more than enough to push the strength of the powerhouses under his command to yet another level.
But what surprised him the most was that among the quest rewards, there was actually a legendary-grade potion!
Daniel placed the [Phantom Potion (legendary-grade)], glowing with a violet radiance, into the guild warehouse.
[Ding! You have sold "Phantom Potion (legendary-grade)" to Doom Guild for 1 copper coin, triggering Millionfold Boost!]
[The item sold belongs to the potion category. Please choose: quality boost / quantity boost!]
"Quality boost!"
[Ding! Congratulations! You have obtained 1 gold coin! You have obtained "Phantom Breath Elixir (supreme-grade)"!]
He took the brand-new potion out of his inventory.
Unlike before, this potion was completely transparent. Inside the bottle was not liquid, but a slowly swirling mass of silver mist, like a compressed galaxy.
[Phantom Breath Elixir (supreme-grade)]

Effect: After use, you may summon ninety-nine clones. Each clone possesses 90% of the original body’s strength. Their range of activity is 5000 × 5000 meters; once they exceed that range, the clones automatically disappear.
Special: The clones inherit all buffs and talent abilities of the original body, and can use skills independently. The clones may also share vision and perception with one another.
Duration: 30 min

Description: According to legend, an ancient God-King refined this potion from fragments of his own soul. One man alone becomes an army of thousands. Drink it, and you yourself will become a force capable of trampling an entire kingdom!
Daniel drew in a deep breath and tilted his head back, swallowing the silver mist in one gulp.
The instant it slid down his throat, he felt as though his consciousness had been torn into countless fragments—only to re-form again in the very next moment.
Except every fragment had become a complete version of himself.
Swish, swish, swish—
Ninety-nine figures stepped out from behind him, standing shoulder to shoulder at his side.
Every single clone held Stellar Wrath in hand, their eyes gleaming with the same calmness and killing intent as his own.
A faint smile rose on Daniel’s lips.
A hundred of himself!
A hundred versions of himself, each possessing 90% of the same Strength, the exact same talents, and the exact same skills.
And with the blessing of Skill Replication, a single cast would be equivalent to forty or fifty thousand attacks!
And once he mastered forbidden spells, one forbidden spell would be the same as tens of thousands of forbidden spells descending at once.
The mere thought of that scene was enough to make one’s scalp go numb.
Daniel did not hesitate in the slightest and threw back his head to drink the potion.
[Ding! You have consumed "Phantom Potion (legendary-grade)"! Talent "Eternal Ring" has been triggered! The potion’s effect has been converted into a permanent effect!]
"Perfect."
He closed the panel, unable to suppress the smile at the corners of his mouth.
With the support of Eternal Ring, this utterly unimaginable effect had now been extended into eternity!
He shut off the status panel, joy surging in his heart.
Just then, a world announcement thundered across the entire Stellar world!
[Server-wide Announcement!!!]
[Player "Faustus" of World Zone No. 616 has completed the main version quest "Twilight of the Empire," opening a brand-new Chapter in the history of the Human Empire!]

[Through the fierce struggle of player "Faustus," the invasions of the shadowkin and the non-human races have been completely crushed! As a special reward, player "Faustus" is hereby granted the title of Grand Duke! At the same time, the Gold Coin drop rate in World Zone No. 616 is increased by 10% for 24 hours!!]
The Multiversal World Channel exploded instantly.
"I’m a player from another zone. Is there any way to switch world zones now?"
"Stop dreaming upstairs. I already checked—no such option exists!"
"This is unfair! Why do all the good things never happen to our zones?!"
"No, seriously, are the GMs of this game blind? They’re just letting that cheating mutt do whatever he wants?"
"World Zone No. 616 is a bunch of bitches, riding the cheater bus and enjoying all the benefits!"
"Fuck you! A bunch of sour-grape losers. Idiots like you will never understand the moves of a god!"
"Exactly! A bunch of frogs at the bottom of a well! All you can do is bark helplessly!"
Daniel took out a scroll glowing with golden light from his inventory.
[Letter of Appointment to Grand Duke (Rare)] (Human Title)
Restriction: Human race only
Privileges:

Any who are granted the rank of Grand Duke stand above all ministers, yielding only to the Emperor alone. Within the Empire, regardless of civil or military status, noble or common, all who hold office must bow in salute upon meeting a Grand Duke. A Grand Duke possesses supreme-grade legal immunity: no blade may touch him, no chain may bind him. Unless more than thirty percent of the Empire’s citizens jointly call for judgment, none may convict him or strip him of his title. Those granted the title of Grand Duke may establish their own official residence and administrative offices, and may independently appoint military commanders and local officials. All subordinate officials shall be recognized under imperial law. They may also issue decree-quests to all citizens of the Empire, with such quests officially notarized by the Empire; all rewards shall be paid by the Grand Duke personally. Those granted the title of Grand Duke may possess the Empire’s highest-tier territories, the "Royal City" class, with no upper limit on number, no restrictions on borders, and no limit on the population or military forces under their jurisdiction.
Description: The title of Grand Duke—granted land enough to stand as a king. From the day of your investiture onward, you shall be the sovereign of this domain and the eternal backbone of humanity.
Daniel carefully read through the description, then used the appointment letter without hesitation.
[Notice: You have successfully obtained the title "Grand Duke"!]
"Grand Duke..."
A faint smile curled Daniel’s lips.
This title was already the pinnacle of the human empire.
One step higher, and he would be Emperor of the Empire.
But that step could not be crossed through merit alone.
Even so, in practical terms, there was not much difference between a Grand Duke and the Emperor.
Within his own territory, he could appoint officials as he pleased and confer titles upon generals at will. To put it simply, he was not much different from a local emperor.
The only difference was that he had to conquer his own land himself.
As long as his strength was great enough, there was no reason he could not seize more territory than even the Emperor!
Immediately afterward, Daniel took out the item he cared about the most from his inventory.
[Key of World (Special Rare)]
Restriction: Usable only in World Zone No. 616
Traits:

This item is indestructible and may be used an unlimited number of times. When your iron hoofs shatter a city of another zone, you may personally annex the entire city—and the land beneath it—into the territory of World Zone No. 616.
Description:
Truth exists only as far as your arrows can reach. Justice exists only where your blade extends.

chapters.title: Chapter 120 -120-Aliris Advances to Transcendent Legendary-grade!
paragraphs: After reading the description, a sharp glint flashed through Daniel’s eyes.
This item was no different from what he remembered.
The only difference was that in his previous lives, it had been controlled by the major guilds—whereas now, it was in his hands.
"This is exactly what I needed."
With a smile at the corner of his lips, he put the item away into his inventory.
With it, forcefully killing World Guardians and forcibly triggering inter-world zone wars would no longer be a problem.
Daniel shifted his gaze to the Ascension Stones in his inventory.
After several major battles in the Abyss Rift and the gains from the battlefield against the non-human races, he now had a total of seventeen Ascension Stones!
Then, without hesitation, he decisively sold them all.
[Ding! You have sold: Ascension Stone (legendary-grade) ×17 to Doom Guild for 1 copper coin, triggering Millionfold Boost!]
[The sold item belongs to the special materials category. Please choose: quality boost / quantity boost!]
"Quality boost!"
[Ding! Congratulations! You have obtained 17 gold coins! You have obtained "Ascendant Starstone (supreme-grade)" ×17!]
Daniel looked at the rainbow-colored crystals glowing in his inventory.
Then his gaze swept across Upton, Theodore, Cole, and Aliris, and in the end, he handed the Ascendant Starstone to Aliris.
A trace of envy flashed through the eyes of high-grade powerhouses like Upton, Cole, and Theodore, but no one said anything.
Because all of them had already used up two Ascendant Starstones in a very short period of time.
But some time had passed since Aliris had first used an Ascendant Starstone.
Using a third one now would not go to waste.
Aliris accepted the Ascendant Starstone, her hands trembling slightly. She took a deep breath, and the crystal in her palm blazed with radiant light.
The next moment—
A pillar of golden light descended from the heavens, enveloping her entire body.
The light was blazing and sacred, as though ancient gods themselves were watching her.
A moment later, the golden radiance faded.
Aliris opened her eyes, and her aura was now completely different—
Transcendent legendary-grade!
Through the succession of great battles, the potential of Daniel’s subordinates had all been stimulated to an astonishing degree.
Aliris in particular had advanced all the way to the peak of high-grade, and now, with the aid of another Ascendant Starstone, she directly broke through into the transcendent realm!
"Thank you, my lord!"
Daniel nodded, and suddenly remembered that there were still ten low legendary-grade powerhouses, granted by the system, waiting for him in Polaris City!
"Back to Polaris City first."
He turned and walked toward the portal.
Polaris City.
The portal lit up one after another.
When Daniel stepped out of the portal, the sight before him made him pause slightly in surprise.
More than fifteen thousand NPC powerhouses stood in perfectly ordered formation across the plaza.
Ten low legendary-grade, five thousand Exalted-grade, and ten thousand epic-grade.
They all knelt on one knee, right hands placed over their left shoulders, heads bowed low in a posture of reverence and solemn respect.
"We greet our lord!"
Their voices boomed like thunder, echoing into the heavens.
Daniel calmly swept his gaze over the assembled ranks.
This batch of mid- and lower-tier powerhouses perfectly filled the deficiencies in the foundation of his faction.
"Carodion."
He turned his head slightly. "Other than the legendary-grade powerhouses, take the rest and arrange accommodations for them."
"As you wish, my lord."
Carodion respectfully accepted the order and led the five thousand Exalted-grade and ten thousand epic-grade powerhouses away.

chapters.title: Chapter 121 -121-The Invasion of the Undead Cataclysm
paragraphs: Memories from his previous life surged back like a tide.
Daniel suddenly recalled that at the very start of the game, a group of players would be chosen by the system and spawned directly into a hidden pocket-world realm.
Everything there existed as a self-contained system, completely cut off from the main world.
Once those players completed the first wave of prerequisite quests for the Undead Cataclysm, they would descend into the main world.
And immediately afterward, the Undead Cataclysm would officially begin.
In his previous lives, after those players from the hidden worlds arrived, a large number of top-ranked experts were pushed off the leaderboards.
Among them, the most dazzling was a player from World Zone No. 1213—Quin!
In the early stages of the game in his previous lives, Quin had been hailed as the number one player in the world, unmatched by anyone!
But in this life, everything would be completely different!
Because Daniel was here!
The title of world number one was destined to belong to him!
Daniel opened the World Rankings.
Sure enough, Quin’s name was right there on the list.
"So they’ve come out after all."
Daniel’s gaze shifted slightly. "If that’s the case, then those experts from World Zone No. 616 should have appeared as well."
With memories from his previous lives, these names were far from unfamiliar to him.
But the impression they had left on him was anything but good.
This group of players caused trouble in the main world every other day, making the players of World Zone No. 616 waste away in several waves of pointless internal conflict.
"Whatever. But if they dare stand in my way, then not even God will be able to save them."
Daniel shook his head, and the smile on his lips turned several degrees colder.
Still, their appearance also meant that the Undead Cataclysm was about to begin!
[Server-wide Announcement!!!]
[The spatial passage between the Undead Realm and Aetheria has been opened! "Undead Cataclysm" is about to descend! Players of all major world zones, prepare yourselves! Countdown: 10 minutes!]
The announcement sounded three times in succession.
After hearing it, Daniel’s expression remained calm as ever.
"As expected. What should come has come."

[Server-wide Announcement: The spatial passage between the Undead Realm and Aetheria has reconnected! "Undead Cataclysm" is about to descend! Players of all major world zones, prepare yourselves—Countdown: 10 minutes!]
[Server-wide Announcement: The calamity quest "Undead Cataclysm" has been forcibly issued to every player! Please check your quest log for details!]
The blood-red announcements exploded three times in a row, like three funeral bells hammering against the heart of every player.
The moment the final words fell, heaven and earth changed abruptly.
The sky, which had been clear and bright only moments before, was swallowed in an instant by boundless darkness.
The sunlight was blotted out by black clouds that surged in from nowhere, the layers of cloud roiling like ink.
The earth sank into a strange, dim yellow gloom. All things lost their original colors, leaving behind only gray-white and dark ochre.
Birds dropped from the sky. Livestock raised by farmers shrieked wildly inside their pens. Even the wind itself seemed to stop breathing.
When the heavens display such ominous signs, disaster or tribulation is sure to follow.
At the same time, the empires of the other world zones fell into unprecedented panic, like anthills thrown into boiling oil.

Countless citizens poured out of their homes and fell to their knees in the streets, between the ridges of farmland, and before the city gates, clasping their hands together and praying toward the sky that had been devoured by darkness.
Some sobbed quietly. Some wailed in despair. Others trembled all over as they recited ancient prayers long since lost to time.
The names of the gods were called again and again in every corner of the world, yet not a single response came.
Some even collapsed to the ground, staring blankly at that black canopy overhead, their faces filled with hopelessness.
They had seen such a sky before—
In the oral tales passed down from their ancestors, and in the yellowed remnants of ancient history books.
Whenever such a sky appeared, it meant that a tide of death and destruction would sweep across the land!
The Imperial Capital, Temple of the Gods.
Swish, swish, swish, swish—
Dozens of golden figures shot into the sky, hovering above the Temple of the Gods.
They stared blankly at the pitch-dark world before them, and the color drained from their faces inch by inch.
"Such dense death energy..."
A white-haired elder muttered hoarsely, his voice like sandpaper scraping across stone. "The scale of this invasion is likely far beyond any before it."
"Ever since the earliest records, the undead race has broken open the spatial passage once every three thousand years to invade Aetheria."
Another middle-aged powerhouse clenched his fists until his knuckles turned white. "Every single time they came, the continent was left littered with corpses and drowned in rivers of blood."
"If not for the countless legendary-grade experts who charged forward wave after wave, there would have been no way to stop the iron hooves of the undead army at all..."
He paused, his voice trembling slightly.

"Especially this time... First we had the allied invasion of the non-human races, then the unsealing of the shadowkin, and now the undead are invading as well. The Empire’s strength has already been weakened considerably."
A transcendent powerhouse let out a long sigh toward the heavens, his eyes filled with indignation and unwillingness.

"Aetheria was only ever a low-tier world to begin with. Its spatial barriers are unbearably fragile. And the divine race forbids us from participating in Heavenscar, making it impossible to solve the problem at its root. Of course this world is plagued by endless calamities!"
"Silence!"
The elder beside him barked sharply, his face turning livid.

"You must not slander the gods! These repeated disasters are trials bestowed upon humanity by the divine race. We have survived every one of them before—at most... it simply costs a few more sacrifices."

The transcendent powerhouse said nothing more, but the hand hanging at his side clenched so tightly that his joints crackled, and the unwillingness in his eyes was so thick it seemed ready to spill over.
The Imperial Capital, the Imperial Palace.
Supported by several ministers, the Emperor trembled as he stepped out of the palace hall and looked up at the sky swallowed by darkness.
His body suddenly swayed, and fortunately the ministers were quick enough to catch him in time.
"First came the invasion of the allied non-human races, then the shadowkin breaking free from their seal..."
The Emperor’s voice was hoarse and exhausted, his eyes heavy with despair. "And now the Undead Cataclysm has arrived as well... Why must our human race suffer so many disasters?"
"Your Majesty, please take care of your sacred health!"
"Yes, Your Majesty! Hundreds of millions of imperial citizens are still depending on you to command the overall situation!"
The old Emperor waved a hand listlessly, as though he had aged another ten years in a single instant.
"I am old... I fear I may not survive this trial."
He looked toward the minister at his side, his voice so low it was almost inaudible.
"Go to the Temple of the Gods and discuss countermeasures with the legendary-grade experts... Come up with a concrete plan as quickly as possible."
He turned around and shuffled back into the hall, his steps slow and unsteady, still muttering under his breath.
"The Empire... truly cannot endure too many more hardships..."
Pyrehaven.
At the portal, white light flashed again and again as dozens of figures stepped out of the radiance.
They stood where they were, their eyes sweeping curiously over everything around them.
Broad stone-paved streets. A towering clock tower. Taverns along the roadside drifting with the scent of ale. In the distance came the rhythmic clang-clang of a blacksmith’s forge.
"So this is the main world..."
One player took a deep breath, as if wanting to carve the smell of the city into his lungs.
"We’ve finally arrived."
"Holy shit, now this feels like a proper game world. I never even got to enter the Starter Village—I was thrown straight into a hidden world instead."
Another player shook his head with a wry smile. "To be honest, I kind of regret that I don’t even know what the village chief of the Starter Village looks like."
"The main world really is better. That hidden world didn’t even have a decent tavern. Boring as hell."
"George, what do we do next?"
"Yeah, George. You’re the strongest among us. Whatever we do from here on, we’ll follow your lead."
Dozens of gazes turned in unison toward the figure standing at the very front of the group!

chapters.title: Chapter 122 -122-An Unbelievable Ranking List
paragraphs: George turned around.
A triumphant smile hung on his lips, as if the whole world ought to bow at his feet.
"Next, we build a guild and recruit people!"
His voice brimmed with unquestionable confidence.
"The Undead Cataclysm is about to arrive. As long as we survive this wave of quests and make a name for ourselves, our guild will take off in no time!"
His gaze swept across the crowd like a blade.
"With our strength, dominating World Zone 616 will be effortless."
He paused, the smile at the corner of his mouth deepening, laced with undisguised disdain.
"That idiot Charles only knows how to put on airs. His sympathy is overflowing so much he’s brought it into the game! Following me is the smartest choice you could make!"
The others all nodded and chimed in, their voices overlapping one after another.
"Brother George is awesome! As expected of the number one player of World Zone 616 in the Hidden World!"
"Well, obviously! George is an SSS-tier talent holder, and he’s got the unique hidden class, Phantom. How could those ordinary players on the main world leaderboards possibly compare to him?"
"Charles may also have an SSS-tier talent, but his hidden class, Holy Light Knight, is only SS-tier. He’s not even in the same league as George!"
Listening to all the flattery, the smile on George’s face only grew broader.
"The system notification just said our levels have entered the main world rankings."
His tone was casual, as though he were mentioning something utterly trivial.
He lifted his chin, a cold gleam flashing through his eyes.
"Then let’s take a look at which World Zone the number one player on the main world leaderboard originally came from."
"Hopefully the players from World Zone 616 aren’t too weak, or that would be pretty embarrassing for us."
Before his words had even faded, George raised a hand and opened the World Level Ranking.
Snowspire.
"Since George doesn’t agree with our ideals, then let them go their own way."
Charles turned around, his eyes falling on the dozens of players who had chosen to stay by his side.
His voice was low and steady, carrying the calm of someone who had been tempered by hardship.
"The Undead Cataclysm is about to descend. This calamity will bring unprecedented destruction to the main world. With our strength alone, there’s no way we can stop it."
He paused before continuing.
"Other than uniting with the player factions of the main world, we have no other choice."
At that moment, a female priest in white robes beside him spoke softly.

"Charles, there’s no need to worry too much. We chose to follow you because we believe in your character and your ability. In the end, you’re the one most qualified to become the leader of the players from World Zone 616."
A gentle smile rose to Charles’s lips, and he nodded at her.
"Thank you for your trust, Cecilia."
He lifted his head, and his gaze turned sharp.
"The system notification just said our levels have entered the world rankings. So let’s see who the top players of World Zone 616 are..."
"Perhaps we can seek their cooperation and fight the coming Undead Cataclysm together."
After saying that, Charles raised a hand and opened the Level Ranking for World Zone 616.
A translucent interface unfolded before George’s eyes.

Rank 1: Faustus (Level 100); World Zone 616; Doom Guild
Rank 2: Skylight (Level 97); World Zone 616; Doom Guild
Rank 3: Sunborn (Level 96); World Zone 616; Doom Guild
Rank 4: White-Headed Fiery Eagle (Level 96); World Zone 616; Eternal Eagle Guild
Rank 5: Quin (Level 96); World Zone 1213
George’s eyes locked onto the name "Faustus," and his pupils contracted sharply.
"Level one hundred?"
His voice was full of disbelief. "How is that possible?!"
It wasn’t just him. The players around him also burst into shocked cries.
"By the gods! What the hell did this Faustus eat to grow that fast? He’s actually level 100!"
"The so-called Unvanquished Fiend, Quin, is only ranked fifth? That’s insane!"
"Exactly! He’s Quin, the player known as the number one in the Hidden World, with the powerful hidden class Violent Fiend, and he’s only in fifth... That’s practically unheard of."
Yet as they continued scrolling down the rankings, every voice abruptly fell silent.
Other than the familiar faces from the Hidden World, among the top tens of thousands of players, ninety-nine percent of the spots were occupied by players from World Zone 616!
What did that mean?
It meant World Zone 616 already possessed the power to crush every other zone with ease.
And not just barely crush them.
It was the kind of overwhelming domination that could be done casually, almost effortlessly.
One player suddenly noticed a common detail and shouted in alarm.
"Holy shit! Look at the guild tags of the World Zone 616 players—most of them are in the same guild!"
"Doom Guild? Damn—this guild’s strength is terrifying! It’s practically ruling all of World Zone 616 by itself!"
"If nothing unexpected happened, then the guild leader should be Faustus, right? He has the highest level..."
George noticed it too.
The rankings were filled, almost uniformly, with the suffix Doom Guild after the names of players from World Zone 616. It was so glaring it was impossible to ignore.
He had never imagined that World Zone 616 could actually dominate the entire Stellar world.
And that even before they had descended here, a behemoth like Doom Guild had already existed.
George was dazed for a moment, murmuring under his breath,
"We weren’t even in the Hidden World for that long... so why does it feel like we’ve come to a completely different world?"
Just then, the players erupted into another round of cries.
"Quick, check the pet rankings—Faustus’s pet is actually legendary-grade!"
"Let me see... fuck, that dragon’s level is even higher than ours!"
"Is this Faustus really that monstrous? Could he be the chairman of some super conglomerate in real life? I wonder who’s stronger, him or Quin?"
"Even though I want Faustus to be stronger, the reality is that Unvanquished Fiend Quin is stronger!"
"Exactly. It’s not that we’re not supporting one of our own—it’s just that Quin can take on ten epic-grade NPCs by himself. With that kind of strength, what is there to doubt?"
As George listened to their discussion, his expression darkened.
In this ranking list, he didn’t even qualify to be compared alongside them.
No matter what, he had still been the number one player of World Zone 616 in the Hidden World!
Level 100. A legendary-grade pet!
The guild leader of the number one guild in World Zone 616!
He clenched his fists tightly in secret, his knuckles turning white, and ground out in a low voice through gritted teeth,
"In the Hidden World, I was already overshadowed by Quin. Now that I’m back in the main world, I’m supposed to be overshadowed by Faustus too?"
"What kind of joke is this?!"
Meanwhile, Charles stared at the level rankings and froze as well.
His mouth fell open, and it took him quite a while to find his voice again.
"This Faustus... is actually level 100? With the class change restriction in place, how could he possibly have leveled that fast?"
"And I... can’t even make it into the top ten."
He wondered if he was hallucinating.
Likewise, the players around him noticed the same thing.
"Holy shit! Is this for real?! That Faustus is actually level 100?"

chapters.title: Chapter 123 -123-The Exalted-Grade Quest, Undead Cataclysm
paragraphs: "Hahahaha... Just thinking about the mighty Quin getting overshadowed is so satisfying!"
"And the one overshadowing Quin is actually a player from our own World Zone 616. Double the satisfaction!"
As Cecilia browsed through the rankings, she suddenly cried out in surprise.
"Did you notice? Players from World Zone 616 actually occupy ninety-nine percent of the leaderboard spots!"
"No way? That exaggerated? I never expected our World Zone 616 to be this powerful, hahaha!"
"With strength like ours, wouldn’t we win future world wars with our eyes closed?"
"Shit, I didn’t even make it into the top hundred. What kind of joke is this?!"
"No, seriously—why are the players from World Zone 616 so absurdly high-level? The number of players in every World Zone should be about the same..."
As he listened to the discussions around him, Charles’s attention settled instead on Doom Guild.
"Look,"
he said, pointing at the rankings, "every World Zone 616 player on the list has the same suffix: Doom Guild."
Prompted by his remark, Cecilia hurriedly looked over as well.
"You’re right! The overwhelming majority of those on the list are Doom Guild members!"
"This guild is incredible. It’s basically unified all the elite-grade players of World Zone 616..."
"Did you notice Faustus, the player in first place?"
"What kind of question is that? He’s the only level 100 player on the board. Seriously, how did he even level like that? Is he cheating?"
"The point is, Faustus is in Doom Guild too. Unless something strange happened, he should be the guild leader."
"Holy shit! Look, Faustus’s pet is level 100 too—higher level than all of us!"
"Let me see... By the gods, it’s even a legendary-grade pet! That’s completely insane!"
Charles quietly listened to the players talking, and a clear plan gradually took shape in his mind.
He turned around, his determined gaze sweeping across the group.
"Everyone, I think we should go speak with Faustus. The Undead Cataclysm is about to descend, and if we want to reduce World Zone 616’s losses to a minimum, we’ll need the strength of Doom Guild."
Cecilia nodded. "I agree!"
"That’s right. We should set out now."
"I second that."
The crowd voiced their agreement in unison.
World Zone 1213.
Roar—!
A thunderous bellow tore through the silence of the sky.
A colossal crimson dragon dived down from the distant clouds, its wings spread wide enough to blot out the heavens. Every scale on its body shimmered with scorching firelight.
It threw back its head and let out a furious roar toward the darkened sky, as if declaring war on the invisible disaster looming above.
Seated cross-legged on the dragon’s back was a young man with long hair flowing over his shoulders.

His features were cold and detached, his brows carrying an aloof arrogance that kept strangers at a distance. In his hand, he held a pitch-black longsword, faint dark-red patterns flowing across its blade.
His gaze pierced through the heavy cloud cover, as if searching for something.
"It’s Quin!"
"So he’s the one known as the Unvanquished Fiend, Quin?"
"That’s him... Damn, aside from that cheat Faustus, I didn’t expect our World Zone 1213 to also have a player who got a giant dragon pet. I’m so jealous!"
"By the way, where did he even get that dragon from?"
"I’m more curious about what he’s trying to do flying up there..."
Quin paid no attention to the chatter below.
His voice, cold as frost, drifted down from the sky.
"The spatial passage to the Undead Realm isn’t here. We’re going to the next main city."
The giant dragon beneath him gave a violent shudder, then spoke in a deep, muffled voice full of resentment.
"Damned human! Forcing me to become your mount was bad enough, but now you even want to order me around and enslave me? You—"
Before it could finish, the dragon suddenly felt an icy chill run down its spine.
It was the instinctive terror of prey being watched by a predator, a fear that shot straight from its backbone to the top of its skull.
It shivered and forcibly swallowed the rest of its complaint.
"Hmph! Then let’s go already!"
With a beat of its wings, the dragon turned into a streak of crimson light and vanished into the horizon.
Polaris City.
Daniel was in the Lord’s Manor checking the quest panel when he suddenly received a message from one of the guild’s high-grade players.
The message said that a player named Charles wished to see him on an urgent matter related to the Undead Cataclysm.
After reading it, Daniel curled his lips into a cold smile.
"Not interested."
In the memories of his previous lives, quite a few players had indeed gathered around Charles, but most of them were ambitious schemers.
Later, they gradually hollowed out Charles’s guild from within, bit by bit devouring its authority.
That guild was mired in internal strife every day, and in the end, it became a laughingstock among the players of World Zone 616.
By contrast, Daniel’s guild was harmonious and orderly inside. No one dared to pull petty tricks.
If Charles and his group got mixed in, there was no telling what kind of chaos they would stir up.
He only wanted to stay far away from people like that.
Cooperate with a bunch of ambitious opportunists?
He had no interest in that whatsoever.
Besides, what they wanted to discuss was nothing more than how to deal with the Undead Cataclysm.
What a joke.
Since when did he need to rely on cooperating with others to complete a quest?
Daniel opened the quest tab.
[Undead Cataclysm (Cataclysm Quest)]
Restriction: All players
Quest Difficulty: Exalted-grade
Quest Objective: Repel this undead invasion

Quest Description: The "hidden pocket world" that once suppressed the passage to the Undead Realm has perished, and the spatial channel between the Undead Realm and Aetheria has reopened. Countless undead creatures will pour forth from the rift and sweep across the entire continent. Their purpose is singular—to devour all civilization!
Every citizen of Aetheria, regardless of origin or strength, bears the responsibility to fight for survival, for their people, and for civilization itself.
Raise the sword in your hand in the name of the eternal human race!
Quest Duration: Long-term
Quest Reward: wish points (the higher your contribution points, the more points you receive)
After reading it, a smile appeared on Daniel’s lips.
"Wish points... now that’s a good thing."
In his previous lives, quite a few players had skyrocketed upward in a single wave thanks to wish points.
As the name implied, the function of wish points was simple:
Whatever you wanted, you could directly exchange for it with wish points!
Of course, that was only if you had enough of them.
The rarer and more precious the item, the more wish points it required.
He rose to his feet and summoned all the legendary-grade powerhouses under his command, then stored them inside the Ring of Void.
With a single thought, thirty figures turned into streams of light and vanished into the depths of the ring.
Daniel unfurled Eternal Black King, black-gold wings glimmering with a cold, ghostly sheen beneath the dim yellow sky.
"The passage to the Undead Realm..."
The corners of his mouth lifted slightly.
"I just so happen to know exactly where it is."
With one beat of his wings, he shot into the sky.
Two minutes later, Daniel hovered above a wasteland a thousand miles beyond Silvermoon Main City.
Within his field of vision stood a colossal gate built entirely from black bones.
The gateway towered over a hundred meters high and spanned more than a hundred meters wide, its entire frame formed from countless unknown, decaying skeletons.
Skulls, ribs, spines, claw-bones...
Every single bone writhed slowly, as if some twisted remnant of life still lingered within them.
The gate had already swung open.
Beyond it lay endless darkness, and within that darkness, countless writhing figures could vaguely be seen.
Rotting corpse claws, pale ghostly hands, and jagged skeletal talons stretched out from the gate, frantically clawing at the air, as if they could not wait to crawl out from that abyss of death.
Black mist poured forth from the doorway in rolling waves. Wherever it passed, grass and trees withered, and the earth cracked open.
Daniel frowned slightly.
The ten-minute countdown mentioned in the announcement had not even ended yet, and these undead creatures were already trying to squeeze their way out.
Once the countdown reached zero, they would surge forth like a tidal wave and drown everything in their path.
He raised his hand and activated the Ring of Void.
Whoosh, whoosh, whoosh—!
Thirty figures appeared out of nowhere.
Carodion, Lucian, Aliris, Tiana...
Thirty legendary-grade powerhouses lined up in a row, hovering behind Daniel.
As they stared at that Blackbone Gate, grave expressions rose in their eyes in perfect unison.

chapters.title: Chapter 124 -124-One Man an Army, the Cataclysm Quest Ends
paragraphs: "So this is... the passage to the Undead Realm."
"The Undead Cataclysm... the most terrifying natural disaster in human history. Every recorded occurrence ended in rivers of blood."
"Sigh... who knows how many living beings will be reduced to ruin this time."
"Then let our flesh and blood become humanity’s first wall!"
Daniel’s expression remained calm.
With a single thought, ninety-nine figures identical to him stepped out from the void.
Ninety-nine clones, each possessing ninety percent of his Strength, skills, and talents.
A hundred figures stood shoulder to shoulder, like an army made up of him alone.
He turned around and looked at the thirty legendary-grade powerhouses behind him.
"As long as we shatter this gate, the Undead Cataclysm in World Zone 616 will vanish before it ever truly begins."
The spirits of the gathered powerhouses were instantly lifted.
Daniel raised Stellar Wrath, golden light condensing along the bowstring.
His voice was calm as still water, yet it carried unquestionable authority.
"Everyone, focus your strongest Strength and attack this gate together."
"As you command, my lord!"
"As you command, sir!"
Thirty voices answered at once, golden radiance igniting on their bodies like thirty stars about to erupt into brilliance.
Daniel was the first to raise Stellar Wrath.
The instant the bowstring trembled, three skills bloomed at the same time.
[Arrowstorm]!
Countless arrows wrapped in raging winds rained down from the sky, each one like a spear of judgment, tearing through the air with a piercing shriek.
[Serpent’s Thundercell]!
Dark clouds gathered in an instant, and tens of thousands of lightning serpents poured downward, violet electricity turning the whole sky as bright as day.
[Shattering Comet]!
A golden arrow shot straight into the heavens, then exploded at its highest point, splitting into thousands of motes of light that dragged brilliant flaming tails as they fell to the earth.
[Aetherlance]!
A golden spear ripped through the sky and shot straight toward the core of the Blackbone Gate.
The ninety-nine clones released their skills in perfect sync with the original body.
A single offensive wave, amplified by all kinds of skills and talents, meant forty to fifty thousand attacks crashing down at once.

Those skills were not multiplying each other exponentially, but the sheer torrent of destructive force was so terrifying that even the all-out strike of a legendary-grade powerhouse would struggle to compare.
At this moment, Daniel’s total damage output was not inferior in the slightest to any peak legendary-grade supreme expert.
It could be said that the current Daniel had already reached the ceiling of the present version.
Before supreme-grade NPCs appeared in the next version, he could basically call himself invincible!
The thirty legendary-grade powerhouses attacked at the same time.
Carodion’s golden sword radiance, Lucian’s silver spear, Aliris’s raging flames...
Countless attacks poured down like a breached flood, completely drowning the Blackbone Gate.
Amid that endless tide of skills, the Blackbone Gate began to tremble.
At first it was only a faint vibration. Then thin cracks appeared on the frame of bones piled up into the gate.
The cracks spread like a spiderweb, accompanied by teeth-gritting cracking sounds.
Daniel did not dare slack off.
His arrows never stopped.
Every draw of the bow unleashed four hundred and fifty attacks.
Seeing their master fight so fiercely, the legendary-grade powerhouses did not dare pause either, and continued pouring out damage like mad.
Several minutes later—
Crack! Crack! Crack!
The entire Blackbone Gate suddenly let out a shrill, ear-piercing noise, as fractures spread across every inch of its surface like a spiderweb.
The rotting bones were stripped away and shattered under the barrage of attacks, turning into black ashes that scattered into the wind.
A faint smile lifted the corner of Daniel’s mouth.
Just then, a sky-shaking roar suddenly came from deep within the Blackbone Gate, filled with fury and unwillingness.
"Which bastard dares destroy my undead spatial passage?!"
"I will never let you off!"
Boom—!!!
The next moment—
The entire Blackbone Gate collapsed with a thunderous crash, dissolving into black mist that scattered into nothingness.
Daniel lowered his bow and stood still, while the ninety-nine clones flowed back into his body like a receding tide.
The thirty legendary-grade powerhouses also stopped attacking at the same time, hovering behind him.
As they looked at the sky, now clear once again, their eyes were filled with disbelief.
They had done it!
They had forcibly destroyed the gate connecting to the Undead Realm!
[Server-wide Announcement!!!]

[Player "Faustus" of World Zone 616 has successfully destroyed the "Undead Realm Spatial Passage"! World Zone 616 has been spared from this civilization-ending calamity, the "Undead Cataclysm"! Special rewards granted to this player: Imperial Morale +100,000, Human Merit +100,000!]

[World Zone 616 Announcement: Player "Faustus," by his own power, destroyed the undead spatial passage and halted the descent of the Undead Cataclysm. Starting today, the nine main cities of World Zone 616 will each establish a "Faustus Plaza" and erect a "Faustus Statue," to stand forever as an example for future generations!]

[World Zone 616 Announcement: Player "Faustus," by preventing disaster before it struck, saved countless citizens of the Empire through his own power. Starting today, all major magic and military academies in World Zone 616, when compiling history, must record Faustus’s glorious deeds in their chronicles, to stand forever as an example for future generations!]
The announcements rang out three times in a row, scarlet letters flashing before the eyes of every player.
Hearing them, Faustus smiled as well.
[Ding! Successfully completed the Exalted-grade quest "Undead Cataclysm." Obtained "wish points" +100,000,000!]
[Imperial Proclamation]

[You now bear the vast destiny of the human race and the Empire, chosen by fate as the helmsman of humanity. From this day onward, the rise and fall of your people, and the direction in which the river of history flows, shall all be written by your hand.
In the eternal name of mankind—may you continue to offer your Strength to the flame of civilization.]
Listening to this string of system notifications, Daniel let out a long breath.
"I didn’t expect to reach this step so quickly."
Luminara.
A grand plaza rose into existence out of thin air.
It was vast and solemn, its ground paved with pure white marble, with nine stone pillars around it carved all over with epic-grade reliefs.
At the very center of the plaza, a towering statue was rapidly taking shape.
It depicted an adventurer dressed as an archer, longbow in hand, head raised toward the sky, eyes filled with determination and unyielding resolve.
On the pedestal of the statue, one name was engraved clearly:
Faustus!
Beneath the name, lines of text slowly appeared, recording his many deeds...

From his first victorious battle in Windmill Town, to suppressing the Mountain God; from crushing the schemes of the beastfolk and goblins, to leading armies against the non-human races; from rising to fame in the battle of Ironforge, to suppressing the Abyss Rift and defeating the alliance of non-human races; and finally, to destroying the spatial passage to the Undead Realm...
Every single deed was a merit worthy of entering the annals of history.
Plazas and statues just like this appeared simultaneously in all nine main cities of World Zone 616.
Countless imperial citizens poured out of their homes and flocked voluntarily toward the newly completed plazas.
They lifted their heads to gaze at that towering statue, at the densely packed list of deeds carved upon its pedestal, their eyes filled with shock and reverence.
